ὀπισθέναρ.definition: the back of the hand, Poll.2.143, 144, 9.126

ὄπισμα.definition: the juice of plants; = Aglaïas23, cf. Sch

ὅπλον.definition: tool, implement, mostly in pl., like; a ship's tackle, tackling, Hom. , 2.390, al., Hes.Op.627; esp. ropes, halyards, etc., Od.2.430, etc.; in which sense Hom. twice uses the sg., rope, 14.346, 21.390: generally, any …

ὀπός.definition: juice, distd. from in that; metaph., the juicy freshness of youth, opp. AP5.257

ὁποσάγωνον.definition: polygon of any number of sides, Papp.314.19

ὁποσταῖος.definition: of what day in serial order, Arat.739

ὁποστημόριος.definition: what fraction, Eudem. ap. Simp.in Ph.973.24

ὁπόστος.definition: in what or which place in numerical order, Archyt.1; what number he had drawn, Pl.R.617e; how many generations from . . , X.Ages.1.2; in a sense determined by the number of which he is one, Arist.Pol.1262a3; . . , D.1…

ὀπόφυλλον.definition: the seed of the Dsc.Eup.1.20, 66, prob. in Dsc.3.80

ὀπτασία.definition: vision, AP6.210 codd. , LXXEs.4.17, Ev.Luc.1.22; simply, appearance, LXXMa.3.2, Si.43.2

Ὀπτιλῖτις.definition: or a name of Athena, Plu.Lyc.11

ὀπτίλος.definition: Dor.for Metop. ap. Stob.3.1.115, Plu.Lyc.11; in IG42.121.40 , al., Hdn.Gr.1.159, 2.560

ὀπτίων.definition: Lat. optio, assistant; esp. in military sense, adjutant or aide-de-camp, Plu.Galb.24, where is f.l., cf. IGRom.4.825 , 3.1131 , Sammelb.6963

ὁραῖος.definition: of a boundary: = gruma, Gloss.; cf

ὀρβικλᾶτον.definition: Lat. malum orbiculatum, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.80f, Dsc.1.115.4

ὄργανον.definition: instrument, implement, tool; organ of sense or apprehension, Pl.R.508b; ib.518c, cf. Tht.185c, al.; Id.Phdr.250b, cf. Ti.45b, Epicur.Nat.11.6,7

ὀργή.definition: natural impulse or propensity; c. gen., visitations of Pan's wrath, Id.Med.1172; but

ὀργιοφάντης.definition: priest, one who initiates others into orgies, AP9.688, Orph.H.6.11

ὀρειάλωτος.definition: wandering on the mountains, condemned by Thom.Mag.p.267 R

ὄρειον.definition: = mare's tail, Hippuris vulgaris, Plin. HN27.115

ὀρειονόμος.definition: = AP6.14 , 240 ; prob. cj. in Anaxil.12; cf

ὄρειος.definition: also Plu.2.965c, Luc.Demon.2, DDeor.20.3; Ep. or from the mountains, mountain-haunting, h.Merc.244, cf. Hes.Fr.198, Phoronis2; this Ep. form is also used by Trag. and Com. in lyr., S.Ant.352, E.IT127,1126, Ph.806, Ar.…

ὀρείτης.definition: name of a stone, Orph.L.362,457; a kind of hawk. Ael.NA2.43

ὄρεξις.definition: general word for all kinds of; c. gen. objecti, longing or yearning after a thing, desire for it, Democr.219, Pl.Def.414b, Arist.EN1119b7, de An.414b6, al.: more rarely, Plu.2.48c; Democr.72

ὀρθαγόρας.definition: pun on a pr. n., with an obsc. allusion, Ar.Ec.916

ὀρθαγορίσκος.definition: sucking-pig, Lacon. word, Ath.4.139b; name of a fish, Apion ap.Plin.HN 32.19

ὀρθάμπελος.definition: a vine growing without props, Plin.HN14.40

Ὀρθάννης.definition: a sort of demon with the attributes of Priapus, Pl.Com.174.12, IG12.52 , Str.13.1.12, cf. Phot. s. v.: written with in IGl.c. and codd. of Pl.Com. and Str., cf. Hdn.Gr.1.70, with in Phot.; in Hsch.; v.l. in Str. l.c.;…

ὄρθαπτον.definition: a woollen cloth for wiping the shrines of temples, Din. ap.Poll.7.69

Ὀρθεία.definition: epith. of Artemis in Laconia and Arcadia ; at her altar the Spartan boys were whipped, X.Lac.2.9, Plu.2.239c:—written IG5.252 ; ib.255.1 ; ib.303.9 ; ib.343.4, al.; ib.22.1623.76 , 5.602.6 ; codd. X., Plu. ll. cc.:—also

ὀρθριοκόκκυξ.definition: early-crower, of the cock, dub. in Diph. ap. Eust.1479.45

ὀρθριοφοίτης.definition: early comer or goer, Phot., Suid

Ὀρθωσία.definition: Ion. = a name of Artemis; a name of Poseidon, Inscr.Délos 440 A61

ὁρίζων.definition: separating circle (cf; Pythag. name for 9, because it limits, i.e. finishes, the series of units, Theol.Ar.57

ὅριος.definition: of boundaries, guardian of; = Lat. Terminus, D.H.2.74, Plu.Num.16

ὁρκάνη.definition: = enclosure, fence, A.Th.346 ; prison, E.Ba.611 , cf. Sch.Theoc.4.61, EM632.25

ὁρκαπάτης.definition: oath-breaker, AP5.249 , Phot., Suid.: as Adj., Nonn.D.48.544

ὄρκυς.definition: acc. a large kind of tunny, Anaxandr.41.62, Archestr.Fr.34.3, Arist.HA543b5, etc.; cf

ὁρμάστειρα.definition: one who urges on, Orph.H.32.9 codd

ὄρμενος.definition: or shoot, sprout, or stem, stalk, = II, esp. = Diph. Siph. ap. Ath.2.62f, Hsch.: pl. Poll.6.61; but also Posidipp.24, cf. Phryn.PSp.67 B.,EM161.4; dat. pl., Jul.Or.5.176a

ὁρμιά.definition: fishing-line of horse-hair, Pl.Com.11, Antiph.28, Arist.HA621a15, S.E.M.9.3, etc. in Babr.6.3 and in qq. v.: metri gr. in dactylic verses, as Theoc.21.11, AP6.4 .]

ὁρμιευτής.definition: angler, un-Att. word in Moer.p.42 P., Hsch

ὁρμιηβόλος.definition: throwing a line, AP6.196 , 7.693 . possible in the former, certain in the latter.]

ὅρμινον.definition: a kind of sage, clary, Salvia Horminum, Thphr.HP8.1.4, Dsc.3.129:—so Polem.Hist.88; in Hsch

ὅρμος.definition: cord, chain, esp. necklace, collar; generally, anything strung like a necklace, wreath, chaplet, Pi.O.2.74; a string of crowns, i. e. of praises, Id.N.4.17

ὄρνεον.definition: = bird, Il.13.64, Cratin.108; the bird-market, Ar.Av.13

ὄρνις.definition: also Il.9.323, 14.290, al., freq. in Att; bird, including birds of prey and domestic fowls, Hom., etc.; applied to ostriches, X.An.1.2.7: freq. added to the specific names, Il.7.59; Od.5.51; S.Aj.629,Fr.323; E.IT1089 …

ὀρνύφιον.definition: Dim. of Thphr.Fr.169, Dsc.2.54, 4.79, Ael.NA4.41, 7.47, Orib.Fr.118; PMag.Leid.V.11.33

ὀρόβακχος.definition: pl., fruits of the pomegranate, Nic.Th.869

ὀροβοειδής.definition: like vetch-seed, of certain urinal; of the colour of vetch, PCair.Zen.92.8, 445.6

ὄροβος.definition: bitter vetch, Vicia Ervilia, Thphr.HP2.4.2; = II, Eust.853.55

ὁρογενής.definition: productive of terms , Iamb.in Nic.p.57 P

ὀρόδαμνος.definition: bough, branch, AP9.3 , Thphr.HP9.16.3, Call.Fr.139, Nic.Th.863, Al.603, etc.:—a shortd. form ; also LXXJb.8.16, Suid., Hsch. , etc.; and Nic.Al.92

ὀροκάρυον.definition: mountain-nut, a tree which grows near the Black Sea, Str.12.3.12

Ὀρομπάτας.definition: epith. of Zeus at Amathus, Hermes 50.158

ὄρον.definition: wooden implement for pressing grapes, A.Fr.107, Is.Fr.24, Men.172; in Poll.7.150, 10.130

ὀρόντιον.definition: name of a plant, a remedy for jaundice, Archig. ap. Gal.13.236

ὀρός.definition: the watery or serous part of milk, whey; the watery part or serum of the blood, Pl.Ti.83d

ὄρουσις.definition: = defined as Stoic.3.40; prob. cj. in Ph.1.602 for

ὀροφή.definition: roof of a house, or ceiling of a; top of a beehive, Arist.HA624a6

ὁροφύλαξ.definition: curator of boundary-stones; frontier-guard, PSI 4.406.12 , SIG633.89

ὀροφύλαξ.definition: mountain-guard, JHS8.236 , Papers of Amer. Sch. at Athens2 No.156 , prob. in MAMA1.123; cf

ὁρρεοπραιποσιτία.definition: office of the horreorum praepositi, IG7.24.7

ὄρρος.definition: end of the os sacrum; generally, rump, Ar.Ra.222, Pax1239, Lys.964, etc. , cf. OE. ears, OHG. ars, etc.: akin also to

ὀρσοδάκνη.definition: an insect which eats the buds of plants, perh. Haltica oleracea, Arist.HA552a30

Ὀρτυγία.definition: Ion. Quail-island, the; part of the city of Syracuse, otherwise called the Island, Str.6.2.4

ὀρυά.definition: a quarrying tool, perh. pickaxe, PCair.Zen.759

ὀρύα.definition: = sausage, name of a play of Epicharmus,p.110 K.: v.l. in Hsch.: Aristarch. ap. Hdn.Gr.1.303 :— hence prob. POxy.1742.9

ὀρυγή.definition: = D.H.4.59, Dsc.4.162, Tz.H.1.915; pl., steps, Cyran.5

ὀρυμαγδός.definition: loud noise, din, as of a throng of men fighting, working, or running about, freq. in Hom. , cf. Hes.Sc.232,401; also of men and dogs, Il.10.185; of horses and men, 17.741: not used of voices, but only of inarticulate …

ὄρυς.definition: a wild animal in Libya, prob. = II.1, Hdt.4.192

ὀρυχή.definition: = Inscr.Délos 365.32; apptly., = snout of a pig, Plu.2.670a

ὀρφανοφύλαξ.definition: one who guards orphans; esp. at Athens, in pl., guardians of orphans who had lost their fathers in war, X.Vect.2.7; cf

Ὀρφεοτελεστής.definition: one who initiates into the mysteries of Orpheus: generally, hierophant, Thphr.Char.16.12, Phld.Po.2.41, Plu.2.224e

ὀρφεύς.definition: = Marc.Sid.33 ; with a pun on Orpheus, Alex.113

Ὀρφεύς.definition: Dor. Ibyc.10A, Hdn.Gr.1.14:— Orpheus, Pi.P.4.177, Pl.R.364e, etc.:—Adj. E.Alc.969 , Pl.Lg.829e; or Hdt.2.81; Arist.de An.410b28

ὀρχάμη.definition: an uncultivated copse, v.l. in Poll.7.147

ὄρχαμος.definition: leader, chief, early Ep. only in the phrases Il.2.837, al., Hes.Fr.96.12, Il.14.102, al.; the former applied to the swineherd Eumaeus, Od.14.22, 121, and the cowherd Philoetius, 20.185,254.—Ep. word, used once by A., …

ὄρχατος.definition: as collective Noun, orchard, garden, Od.7.112, cf. 24.222, al.; AP9.314

ὀρχίλος.definition: a bird, prob. wren , Ar.Av.568, V.1513, Arat.1025; a bird of ill omen at weddings, Euph.4; in Arist.HA609a12, Thphr.Sign.39, 53, proparox

ὄρχις.definition: and Att. nom. pl. Ion; in females, ovaries, Gal.2.810, al

ὄρχος.definition: a row of vines or fruit-trees; = rim of eyelid, Poll.2.69

ὁσάγωνος.definition: of whatever number of sides, Theo Sm.p.40 H

ὄσιρις.definition: poet's cassia, Osyris alba, Dsc.4.140 , Gal.12.93, Plin.HN27.111

ὅσος.definition: Ep. both forms in Hom. and Hes; with a partit. gen. in the principal clause, Il.12.13; 5.267; A.Pers.441; . . of all the Achaeans, Il.9.55; which are and which are not . . , Pl.R.467d; on v. A.III

ὄσπριον.definition: pulse of all kinds, Hdt.2.37, Alex.266.7, Thphr.HP8.1.1, PPetr.3p.261 , Gal.6.302, etc.: mostly in pl., Hp.Acut.47, X.An.4.4.9, Pl.Criti.115b, Orib.Fr.142.—cf

ὄσσα.definition: Att. a rumour, which, from its origin; generally, voice, of the Muses, Hes.Th.10,43,65; of a bull, ib.832

ὁσσίχος.definition: Dim. of as little, how little, Theoc.4.55, Hsch

ὀστακός.definition: = lobster, Aristomen.6, Eun.Hist.p.251 D.: as pr. n. Inscr.Délos442A20

ὀστάριον.definition: Dim. of little bone, PTeb.1.18; stone, kernel, of nuts, etc., Id.1.118, Alex.Trall.8.2, Paul.Aeg.6.24

ὀστέϊνος.definition: made of bone, of bone, Hdt.4.2, Pl.Ti.74a, Arist.HA493a2; cf

ὀστέον.definition: Att. contr. poet. AP7.480; metaph., i.e. rocks, Choeril.Trag.2

ὄστινος.definition: Att. form of acc. to Poll.2.232, Phot., found in Arist.PA692b18 codd., Gal.18.237; bone-pipes, Ar.Ach.863

ὀστίτης.definition: in or of the bones, Ruf.Onom.217

ὄστλιγξ.definition: hair, esp. curled hair, lock of; anything curled or twisted, as

ὄστρακον.definition: earthen vessel, Ar.Ra.1190, Ec.1033; fragment of such a vessel, potsherd, IG42.121.82 , LXXPs.21.16, al., Ostr.1152, etc.; Hp.Morb.2.47; esp. the potsherd used in voting : hence the danger of ostracism is past, Cratin…

ὀστρέϊνος.definition: of or living in a shell, testaceous; purple, in form POxy.109.5

ὄστριμον.definition: byre or enclosure for cattle, Antim.41, cf. Lyc.94 : Hsch

ὀστρύα.definition: and hop hornbeam, Ostrya carpinifolia, Thphr.HP3.10.3, cf. 3.3.1, 3.6.1, Plin.HN13.117; also Thphr.HP1.8.2

ὀσφυήξ.definition: having dislocated one's hip, Poet. ap. Lex. de Spir.p.209 V

ὀσφῦς.definition: gen. acc. also AP12.213; Hellenist., metaph., of a son, Act.Ap.2.30, cf. LXXGe.35.11, al

ὄσχη.definition: scrotum, Hp.Morb.2.61 and 71, al.; but in; = Nic.Al.109, cf. Hsch. [Accent acc. to Hdn.Gr.2.121.]

ὄσχιον.definition: raised margin of the womb, Gal.19.127; cf

ὄσχις.definition: said to be = Hp.Coac.528; but as the reference is to a male in Id.Epid.7.33 Littré's cj. should be accepted in both places, as also for in ib.5.61

ὀτεῖος.definition: Cret. for but in sense, = Leg.Gort.4.52, 5.1, Schwyzer 183.5 :—Boeot. in ; cf

ὄτλος.definition: suffering, distress, arising from a thing, A.Th.18; S.Tr.7

ὀτραλέος.definition: = Opp.H.2.273, Q.S.11.107:— used by Hom. and Hes. only in Adv. quickly, readily, Il.3.260, Od.19.100, Hes.Sc.410, Sapph.Supp.20a.11, A.R.1.1210

ὄτταβος.definition: given as a form of EM615.57

ὀττεία.definition: divination from ominous sounds, D.H.8.37; Id.9.45; evil foreboding, Id.1.38

οὐγγία.definition: or Lat. uncia, as adopted by the Sicil. Greeks, Arist.Fr.510, Gal.13.789, Alex.Aphr.in Top.210.7:—written in Epich.203, Sophr.151: hence Adj. of one uncia, prob. in SIG1042.23 : measurement by unciae, in pl., Just.Nov…

οὐδαῖος.definition: and on the ground, Orph.A.394; like under the earth, infernal, of Persephone, Lyc.49, 698; of Zeus, AP14.123 , D.P.789

οὖδας.definition: gen. dat. Il.5.734, al. (more; floor, pavement in rooms and houses, Od.23.46; on the floor of Zeus' abode, Il.24.527; 5.734, 8.385: prov., to bring a man to the pavement, i.e. to strip him of all he has, h.Merc.284

οὐδενόσωρος.definition: worth no notice or regard, . . Il.8.178; Opp.H.2.478

οὐδός.definition: Dor. Berl.Sitzb.1927.170; generally, threshold, entrance to any place, Od.1.104; to the nether world, Il.8.15; S.OC57, cf. 1590: in pl., perh. lintel, Theoc.23.50

οὐδών.definition: a kind of felt shoe, Poll.10.50: Dim. Edict.Diocl. in IG5.1406.24 :—also Charis.1.552 K., Gloss

οὐένετος.definition: Lat. venetus, of the faction of the Blues in the chariot races, Tab. Defix.Aud.234.5 :—also ib.237.6; cf. D.C.61.6, 77.10

οὐετερανός.definition: = Lat. veteranus, IGRom.3.140 , etc.; also ib.99, 142, etc.; written in Zonar

οὖθαρ.definition: prop. of animals, udder, Od.9.440, Hdt.4.2, Theoc.8.42,69, etc.; Arist.HA523a1; distd. from by Plu.2.496c; eaten as a dish, ib.124f; later of women, breast, A.Ch.532; Telecl.31. II. metaph., the richest, most fertile …

οὔϊγγον.definition: Egyptian arum, Colocasia antiquorum, Thphr.HP1.1.7, 1.6.9, 11; cf. Hsch

οὐΐτουλος.definition: the Lat. vitulus, Hellanic.111 J., as root of Italia

οὐλάς.definition: pecul. fem. of , crisped; as Subst., = Call.Fr.360 , cf. Hsch. s. vv. Phot., Sch.Theoc.1.53; restd. for in AP7.413

οὐλή.definition: wound scarred over, scar, Od.19.391,393, al. , E.El.573, Hp.Morb.1.21, PGrenf.2.32.5 , etc.; X.Mem.3.4.1; Pl.Grg.524c; . . , D.53.8; Arist.Pr.877a2: metaph., Plu.2.65d

οὐλόμενος.definition: ruined, lost: hence, unhappy, wretched, A.Ch.152; in lit. sense, E.Or.1307; Id.IT1109; . . Id.IA792 ; Aeol. dub. sens. in Alc.Oxy.1788 Fr.4.20

οὖλον.definition: mostly in pl., the gums, A.Ch.898, Hp.Epid.7.113, Aph.3.25, Morb.2.11, Pl.Phdr.251c, Nic.Th.306, etc.: sg., Arist.HA493a1, D.L.7.176

οὐλοπρόσωπος.definition: with scars on the face, AnatoliusinCat.Cod. Astr.8.188.6

οὖλος.definition: old Ep. and Ion. form of whole, entire, v; woolly, of thick, fleecy wool

οὐλότης.definition: curliness, woolliness, opp. Arist.GA782a3,b28, Pr.909a30; Philostr.Im.2.6; close-grained texture, Thphr.CP6.11.8, cf. HP5.2.3, etc

οὐλοφυής.definition: rough, raw, undifferentiated, of lumps of earth , Emp.62.4

οὐλόφυλλος.definition: with curling leaves, opp. of cabbage, Thphr.HP7.4.4

οὔπιγγος.definition: a hymn to Artemis, Ath.14.619b, Poll.1.38; at Troezen, acc. to Did. ap. Sch.A.R.1.972

Οὖπις.definition: name of Artemis, Call.Dian.204; later, epith. of Nemesis, IG14.1389ii 2

οὐρά.definition: Ion. tail, of a lion; = S.Fr.1078, f.l. in Hom.Epigr.12

οὐραῖος.definition: tail, Achae.27.3; Men.Kol.Fr.7; E.Ion1154; in fish, tail- fin, S.Fr.762, Arist.HA490a4, al., dub. l. in Arat.363; hinder part, rear, Ph.2.109, Luc.VH1.35, 2.1

Οὐρανιάς.definition: [celebration of] games in honour of Urania, IG5.659, 662

Οὐρανίδης.definition: Dor. son of Uranos, Hes.Th.486; Pi.P.3.4; the Titans, Hes.Th.502; the gods, Pi.P.4.194, Cerc.4.39, Call.Jov.3, etc

οὐρανός.definition: Dor. and Boeot. Alcm.23.16; heaven: in Hom. and Hes

οὖραξ.definition: gen. Att. name of the bird , Arist.HA559a12

οὐραχός.definition: urachus, a foetal organ connected with the; apex of the heart, Hp.Cord.4, cf. Aret.SA1.8

οὔρειος.definition: Ep. for II. for urine, Antisth. ap. Phot.; Hsch; for urine, Antisth. ap. Phot.; Hsch

οὐρεύς.definition: Ion. for : in Il.1.50, 10.84 it has been taken as, = a guard, warder, cf. Arist.Po.1461a10; but it may well mean mules here, as in other places, and the Sch. give both explanations

οὐρίαχος.definition: bottom, butt-end; part of an oar, Poll.1.90

οὐριβάτας.definition: poet. for walking the mountains, E.Fr.773.27 , cj. in Id.El.170

οὔριος.definition: also S.Ph.355: :—with a; metaph., prosperous, successful, A.Ch.814 , cf. E.HF95; Id.Heracl.822; AP7.164.10 : neut. pl. as Adv., E.Hel.1588

οὐριοστάτης.definition: steady and prosperous, A.Ch.821 :—a dub. passage

οὐροβόρος.definition: devouring its tail, PMag.Lond.121.587, PMag.Osl.1.184, Olymp.Alch.p.80 B.; cf

οὖρον.definition: urine, Hdt.2.111, etc.: pl., Hp.Aph.4.69,72, Thphr.Od.60; limit, range, Il.23.431, cf. the range of mules, i.e. the breadth of land ploughed in a day by mules, the length of the furrow being fixed, 10.351: so in sg., …

οὖρος.definition: fair wind, . . Od.11.7, cf. 15.292, Il.1.479, etc.; . . , Od.4.357; 5.167; ib.268; Pi.P.1.34; E.Tr.20; Theoc.13.52; Od.5.176, etc. ; the gods changed the wind again to a fair one, Od.4.520: pl., ib.360; later, send do…

οὐρός.definition: trench or channel for hauling up and launching ships, Il.2.153, cf. Poll.10.149

οὔσκη.definition: glossed in margin by Zos.Alch.p.222 B

οὖσον.definition: ship's tackle, ropes, Lyc.20 , Alex.Aet.3.21, pl. prob. in Antim. Col.6

ὄφελμα.definition: increase, advantage, S.Fr.1079; broom, Hippon.51, Eust.1887.34, Hsch

ὄφελος.definition: only in nom. and acc. sg; all that is best, all the best people, Ar.Ec.53, cf. Luc.Herod.8: c. gen., the serviceable part of the army, X.HG5.3.6, cf. Theoc.13.18; . . the flower of gluttony, Luc.Tim.55

ὀφεωπλόκαμος.definition: with serpent hair, Corn.ND10 , PMag.Par.1.2863 , Eust.716.57

ὀφθαλμός.definition: temporary loss of sight, Gal.17.400; in sg., the eye of a master or ruler, Hes.Op.267; Men.Mon.179; X.Oec.12.20; of God, Secund.Sent.3; so a king is called A.Ch.934 ; and in Persia the king's eye was a confidential of…

ὀφίδιον.definition: Dim. of IG22.1533.16; a kind of fish, Plin.HN32.149; cf. Hsch. (Prob. contr. fr

ὀφιηβοσίη.definition: food of serpents, of the Pythian laurel and the Nemean celery, Inscr.Cos58.5

ὀφίουρος.definition: serpent-tailed, of an Ethiopian bird, Hsch

ὀφιοῦχος.definition: the constellation Ophiuchus; a who interferes with alchemists, Olymp.Alch.p.86 B

ὄφις.definition: gen. poet. also E.Supp.703; like a serpent-like bracelet, Men.387, Nicostr. Com.33, Philostr.Ep.22; is Att. for acc. to Moer.p.288 P

ὀφίτης.definition: of or like a serpent; = shingles, Gal.19.440

ὀφίων.definition: mousmon, the wild sheep of Sardinia, Plin.HN28.151, 30.146

ὀφρύη.definition: Ion. for II, Hdt.4.181,182,185; also in E.Heracl.394: written in PHal.1.84 , cf. Hsch.: Dor. Schwyzer89.14

ὀφρῦς.definition: acc. in late Poets; alone, scorn, pride, AP7.409 , 9.43 , 10.122 , etc

ὀχεά.definition: Ion. = cave, grot, Arat.1026, Nic.Th.139, Orph.A.79: contr. gen. Arat.956. [Oxyt. acc. to Theognost.Can.102.]

ὀχετός.definition: means for carrying water; in Anatomy, ducts leading to the lungs, Pl.Ti.70d; Poll.2.217; of the urinal and intestinal canals, Hp.Art.48, 50, X.Mem.1.4.6; , Hp.Epid.6.3.1

ὄχευμα.definition: result of the embryo, Arist.HA577a26, prob. cj. in Ph.2.506

ὀχεύς.definition: Ep. anything used for holding; band or strap for fastening the helmet under the chin, Il.3.372

ὄχθη.definition: older form of any height or rising ground, natural or artificial, bank, dyke by the side of a river, Il.21.171, cf. 172: in sg., also, Plu.Publ.16, Arr.An.1.14.4, CPHerm. 95.10 : mostly in pl., raised banks of a river…

ὄχθοιβος.definition: purple stripe down the front of the; neckband, IG12.387.35, cf. 22.1388.84, 1400.67; ib.1425.309

ὄχθος.definition: eminence, bank, hill, first in h.Ap.17; tubercle in leprosy, Aret.SD2.13, Ruf. ap. Orib.45.28.3

ὀχθοφύλαξ.definition: watchman on a river-bank, Lat. riparius, Gloss

ὄχλος.definition: in political sense, populace, mob, opp. , Th.7.8, cf. Pl.Plt.304d; Id.Ax.368d; X.Cyr.2.2.21; and popular assemblies , Pl.Grg.455a, cf. Euthd.290a: prov., this is already in the mouths of the people, D.H.Lys.10, cf. J.…

ὄχος.definition: carriage, used by Hom. in heterocl; the swift or round bearers of the chariot, i.e. the wheels, E.IA146

ὀχυρότης.definition: firmness, strength, esp. of a stronghold or country, Aen. Tact.22.2, cf. J.AJ3.14.2: pl., Plb.5.62.6,7.15.2

ὄψ.definition: poetic Noun, used in obliq. cases of sg; gen. = the eye, face, Emp.88, Antim.63

ὀψαμάτης.definition: Dor. for one who mows till late at even, Theoc.10.7

ὀψία.definition: Ion. , the latter part of day, evening, opp. freq. joined with , Hdt.7.167; Th.8.26; late in the evening, D.57.9; alone, POxy.528.5 .—Cf

ὀψιανὸς λίθος.definition: a black stone, perh. obsidian, Pliny's obsiana , HN36.196, cf. Peripl.M.Rubr.5, Orph.L.285, Cyran.26: written PLeid.X.36 B.; dub. in Supp.Epigr.2.776 i 15

ὄψιμος.definition: poet. for late, slow, for a late time, Il.2.325: in Prose, late in the season, X.Oec.17.4, 5, but f.l. for in Thphr.HP1.9.7, al.; of crops, LXXEx.9.32, PSI4.433.2 , PCair.Zen.299.2 ; D.S.1.10; Ep.Jac.5.7: Comp., PFay.…

ὀψίνοος.definition: late-observing, i.e. remiss, inobservant, of Epimetheus, Pi.P.5.28

ὄψιος.definition: Att. Comp. later, Id.Mete.362a24, al., Thphr.CP1.10.5: Sup. X.HG5.4.3: hence as Adv., Comp. of Pl.Cra.433a, Thphr.HP3.2.1, Eub.119.11: Sup. opp. Pl.Prt.326c, X.HG4.5.18, etc.: also Comp. as v.l. in Thphr.: also shortd…

ὀψιπέδων.definition: one who has long been in fetters, Men.1049

ὄψις.definition: objective, aspect, appearance of a person or thing, Il.6.468; 24.632, cf. S.Ph.1412 ; Id.OC577; made the appearance greater, Th.6.46; PCair.Zen. 157.4 ; X.An.5.9.9; Th.1.10; Id.7.44: the acc. is used abs., in appearan…

ὄψον.definition: cooked or otherwise prepared food, a made; relish, Il.11.630; . . pudding and knuckle-sauce, Ar.Pax123: metaph., 'hunger is the best sauce', X.Cyr.1.5.12; Id.Mem.1.3.5; Socr. ap. Porph.Abst.3.26; X.Cyr.7.5.80

ὀψώνιον.definition: salary, reckoned in money; a policeman's pay, PLille25.55 , PFay.302 , IG9.1109.27 ; freq. a soldier's pay, PStrassb.103.16 , PTheb.Bank6.7 , Plb.6.39.12: so in pl., pay of an army, Rev.Ét.Anc.33.8 , OGI 229.106 , SIG…

ὀαρίζω.definition: Ep. Verb, used only in pres. and impf., converse or chat with , c. dat. pers., Il.6.516; 22.127; h.Merc.170: c.acc. cogn., h.Hom.23.3: contr. impf., h.Merc.58

ὀαρισμός.definition: = foreg., in pl., Hes.Op.789; Call.Fr.118: in sg., Q.S.7.316

ὀαριστής.definition: familiar friend, . . Od.19.179, cited by Pl.Min.319d; . . Timo57

ὀαριστύς.definition: Ep., = familiar converse; as concrete, the company of out- fighters, 13.291

ὄαρος.definition: song, ditty, Pi.P.4.137; an oblique, i. e. biassed, song, Id.N.7.69: pl., Id.P.1.98, N.3.11: in later Poets mostly of lovers, AP9.362.16; ib.10.68 , Musae.132, etc

ὀβάλλω.definition: thrust through, Hsch.: perh. from cf

ὀβελεία.definition: an unknown iron object, in pl., IG22.1631.409, 1672.310: sg., in a list of cups, etc., prob. in ib. 1695.14, 15

ὀβελία.definition: perh. a tax of an obol, SIG1000.3

ὀβελιαῖος.definition: sagittal, of a suture of the skull, Gal.14.720; of an incision, straight, Paul.Aeg.6.8

ὀβελίας ἄρτος.definition: roll or loaf baked or toasted on a spit, Hp.Vict.2.42, Ar.Fr.103, Ph.2.273, cf. Moer.p.287 P.; without Pherecr.55, Nicopho15:—also CIG3597b ; and . But in AB111 we have .— Ath.3.111b writes it and gives both interpret…

ὀβελιαφόρος.definition: carrying Poll.6.75: in pl., title of play by Ephippus

ὀβελίζω.definition: mark with a critical obelus , Cic.Fam.9.10.1, Hermog.Id.2.3:—Pass., ibid

ὀβελισκολύχνιον.definition: spit used as a lampholder , Theopomp. Com.7, Arist.Pol.1299b10, PA683a25

ὀβελίσκος.definition: Dim. of I, small spit, skewer; nail, IG12.313.141 , 11.148.70

ὀβελός.definition: pointed square pillar, obelisk, Hdt.2.111, 170, Jul.Ep.59; = IG12.6.95, al., Milet.7.59:—so in Dor. form Leg.Gort.2.14, GDI5011.5 , ib.2561 D 27, al. , etc.: Thess. IG9.1229.20

ὀβολιαῖος.definition: of the weight of an obol, Arist.HA522a31, Gal.13.101; worth an obol, i. e. petty, TheanoEp.6.2

ὀβολίσκος.definition: perh. = IV, PSI6.698.16 (iv A; part of a ship's tackle, PLond.3.1164h 11

ὀβολοστατέω.definition: weigh obols : hence, practise petty usury, Lys.Fr.60, Luc.Nec.2

ὀβολοστάτης.definition: weigher of obols, i.e. petty usurer, Ar.Nu.1155, Hyp.Fr.154, Antiph.168, Philostr.VA8.7, Onos.1.20; but Sch.Aeschin.1.39: perh. from = cf. and Hsch. s. vv. Pl.Ax.367b, Poll.3.112: hence , the trade of a petty usurer, …

ὀβριμοδερκής.definition: with mighty glance, of Athena, B.15.20

ὀβριμόθυμος.definition: strong of spirit, Hes.Th.140, h.Hom.8.2: written Orph.Fr.169.12

ὀβριμοπάτρη.definition: daughter of a mighty sire, epith. of Athena, Il.5.747, al., Hes.Th.587, Sol.4.3: Ar.Eq.1178:—also Corn.ND21

ὄβρυζος.definition: pure, of gold, PLips.63.11 , cf. PKlein.Form.393 , al.; Sch.Th.2.13, etc

ὀγδοαῖος.definition: on the eighth day, Plb.5.52.3, al; of fever, recurring on the eighth day, octavan, Id.7.505

ὀγδοάς.definition: the number eight, Plu.2.744b; group of eight, IG 3.1308; the eighth heaven, Basilid. ap. Hippol.Haer.7.27: pr. n. of a deity, PMag.Leid.W.17.5, cf. 16.46

ὀγδόατος.definition: poet. for as for the eighth, Il.19.246, Od.3.306, Emp.68; Rev.Phil.22.357; the eighth day, octave, Hes.Op.772, 790 )

ὀγδοηκοντάλιθος.definition: title of work by Orpheus, Suid. s.v

ὀγδοηκοντάρουρος.definition: having tenure of eighty PTeb. 63.40 , etc

ὀγδοημόριον.definition: eighth part, Inscr. Délos504A 12 , Theol.Ar.4, Mnesith. Cyz. ap. Orib.inc.15.12:—also IG11.203 A59, 71 , PSI6.595.7

ὀγκάομαι.definition: bray, of the ass, Theopomp.Com.4, Arist.HA609a33, Call.Aet.Oxy.2079.31, Luc.DMar.1.4

ὀγκηθμός.definition: braying, of the ass, Luc.Asin.15, Gloss; lowing, of the ox, Nonn.D.5.71

ὀγκηστής.definition: brayer, AP9.301 , cf. Epigr. ap. Gal.Protr.13

ὀγκολογέω.definition: speak in a hollow voice, = Hsch

ὀγκόω.definition: aor. aor. and pf. Pass; distend, Arist.Somn.Vig.457a13, cf. Pr.936b11:—Pass., was swollen by eating, Babr.86.5, cf. 111.19, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.3

ὀγκύλλομαι.definition: Pass., = to be swollen, Hp.Prorrh.1.99, Coac.606: metaph., to be puffed up, Ar.Pax465; Ath.9.382b

ὀγκυλόομαι.definition: Pass., = in pf. part. Hp. ap. Erot., cf. Suid

ὄγκωμα.definition: swelling, Gal.16.720, Sch.Ar.Pax540; elbow, prob. f.l. for Orib.45.15.1, Eust.1397.5

ὀγμεύω.definition: move in a straight line, prop. of ploughers or mowers, Hsch. s.v. metaph., c. acc. cogn., plough or trail one's weary way, of a lame man, S.Ph.163 ; they were marching in file before him, X.Cyr.2.4.20

ὁδαῖος.definition: = of Hermes, Id; that for which a merchant travels, merchandise , Od.8.163, 15.445; though a Sch. explains it as = Lat. viaticum; cf

ὀδακτάζω.definition: bite, gnaw, Call.Del.322, A.R.4.1608: D.H.14.10; cf

ὀδαξησμός.definition: = Hp.Aph.3.25, Ph.2.301, Dsc.2.72, Plu.2.769e, Aret.CA1.2, Ael.NA1.38, Artem.5.67

ὀδάξω.definition: impf. X.Smp.4.28:—more freq. in Med; Hsch.; cause irritation, AB340, Suid., Phot. ; irritants, Hp.Mul.1.18 codd. opt.: fut. ib.2.154: pres. is an irritant, ib.160; Id.Gland.13: c. acc., nibbled at it, AP9.86

ὁδάω.definition: export and sell: generally, sell, E.Cyc.98; ib.133:—Pass., to be carried away and sold, ib.12:—also Hsch.—Cf

ὁδεύσιμος.definition: passable, practicable, Id.11.7.5, Max. Tyr.39.3, Gloss

ὁδεύω.definition: c. acc. loci, travel over, A.R.4.1441; Plu.Eum.15; IG 14.2012A36; . . Epigr.Gr.226.3 :— Pass., thoroughfare, highway, POxy. 1537.18 , Stud.Pal.20.117.6

ὁδηγέω.definition: lead one upon his way, guide, c. acc. pers., Ps.-Phoc.24, A.Pr.728, Act.Ap.8.31, X.Eph.1.9: abs., E.HF1402; Hp.Lex2:—Pass., Plu.2.954b, Vett. Val.359.30:— also Them.Or.11.151c

ὁδηγός.definition: guide, Plb.5.5.15, Plu.Alex.27; of a goddess, Paus.2.11.2; part of a dirigible Ath.Mech.34.6; D.H.Amm.1.12, cf. Phld.Lib.p.20 O.: as Adj., pilot-boats, Sammelb.7173.16

ὅδιος.definition: belonging to a way or journey; travelling expenses, prob. in Inscr.Magn.52.39

ὅδισμα.definition: a way compact with bolts, i.e. Xerxes' bridge over the Hellespont, A.Pers.71

ὁδίτης.definition: wayfarer, traveller, Od.7.204, 17.211, S.Ph.147; Il.16.263; Dor. Theoc.16.93

ὁδοιδόκος.definition: footpad, highwayman, Plb.13.8.2, Posidon.36 J., D.Chr.4.95

ὁδοιπορέω.definition: impf. Hdt.4.116 , S.OT1027: fut. Hp.Art.58: pf. Philippid.13: plpf. 3pl. Hdt.8.129:—Pass., pf. Luc.Herm.2:— walk, Hdt.4.110, S.OT801; Hp. l.c.; walk on tiptoe, S.Aj.1230; come, . . Id.OC1251: c. acc. cogn., Hdt.4.116;…

ὁδοιπορία.definition: Ion. walking, h.Merc.85, Hp.Fract.15 , Hdt.2.29,8.118; X.Cyr.1.2.10; the uncertainty of the journey by road, POxy.118v.6 ; power of walking, Nonn.D.25.552; journey, IG22.2640

ὁδοιπόριον.definition: passagemoney paid to a ship-master, or provisions for the voyage, Od.15.506: pl., Sammelb.7243.5

ὁδοιπόρος.definition: wayfarer, traveller, Il.24.375, A.Ag.901, S.OT292, Ar.Ach.205, Stratt.61, IG42.121.83

ὀδοντάγρα.definition: Ion. forceps for drawing teeth, Hp.Medic.9, Arist.Mech.854a17, Plu.2.468c, Sor.2.63, Gal.17.911

ὀδοντίζω.definition: polish with a tooth, PLeid.X.8 B., al; furnish with teeth, in Pass., a cogged wheel, Orib.49.4.43; cf. gloss on in Hp.Art.8

ὀδοντισμός.definition: a mode of playing the flute, in which the gnashing of the teeth of the serpent Pytho was imitated, Poll.4.80,84

ὀδοντοειδής.definition: tooth-shaped, the odontoid process, Gal.2.757, cf. 17.374

ὀδοντόκερας.definition: horn-tooth, i.e. tusk, of an elephant, Amynt. ap. An.Ox.3.357

ὀδοντοξέστης.definition: instrument for cleaning the teeth, Poll.2.96

ὀδοντόομαι.definition: Pass., to be furnished with teeth, Poll.2.96, Gloss

ὀδοντότριμμα.definition: = foreg., Damocr. ap. Gal.12.890, Gal.12.884, An.Par.1.394, Gloss

ὀδοντοτύραννος.definition: a large animal, prob. crocodile, in the Indus or Ganges, Ps.-Callisth.3.10

ὀδοντοφόρος.definition: bearing teeth, an ornament for horses, consisting of strings of teeth, AP6.246

ὀδοντοφυέω.definition: cut teeth, Hp.Aph.3.25, Pl.Phdr.251c, Arist.HA587b15, al

ὀδοντοφυής.definition: sprung from the dragon's teeth, of the Sparti, E.Ph.821

ὀδοντοφυΐα.definition: Ion. teething, Hp.Dent.6, al., Poll.2.96, Jul.Or.7.206d, Herm.in Phdr.p.161 A., Paul.Aeg.1.9

ὁδοποιέω.definition: impf. X.An.4.8.8: plpf. with; metaph., pave the way, Arist.Metaph.984a18

ὁδοποιία.definition: roadmaking, the work of a pioneer, X.Cyr.6.2.36, IG22.1673.28, PGrenf. 2.14.6 , Plu.CG7:—written Supp.Epigr.4.447.28

ὁδοποιός.definition: one who opens the way, road-maker, pioneer, X.Cyr.6.2.36,J.BJ3.6.2; road-surveyor, Aeschin.3.25,Arist.Ath.54.1 ; courier, POxy.1656.1

ὁδοσκοπέω.definition: watch the roads, of footpads, Eust.1445.19

ὁδοφυλακέω.definition: watch or guard the roads, Phot.s.v

ὁδοφύλαξ.definition: watcher of the roads; = II, Eust.1445.20

ὁδόω.definition: lead by the right way, A.Pr.813; ib.498: c. inf., who put mortals on the way to wisdom, Id.Ag.176 ; of things, direct, ordain, E.Ion1050 :—Pass., to be on the right way, Hdt.4.139

ὀδυναίτερος.definition: irreg. Comp. form of or Hp.Fract.17

ὀδυνάω.definition: aor. Gal.10.853:—Pass., Phld.Lib.p.29 O.; 2sg. Ev.Luc.16.25: fut. Gal.10.851, but Men.325.16, TelesFr.2p.9H.: aor. Ar.Ach.3:— cause one pain or suffering, E.Hipp.247 , cf. Ar.Lys.164; Id.Ec.928; Men.659:—Pass., feel p…

ὀδύνη.definition: pain of mind, grief, distress, once in Il., grief for him, 15.25: more freq. in Od., always in pl., 1.242; 2.79,al.: after Hom. the pl. was most common in both senses, S.Tr.959, 986 ; Ar.Ach.526; opp. Antipho Soph.49;…

ὀδυνήφατος.definition: killing, i. e. stilling, pain, Il.5.401,900, cf. 11.847, Orph.L.345, 753

ὄδυρμα.definition: complaint, wailing, mostly in pl., A.Ch.508, S.Tr.50, etc.: in sg., E.Tr.1226

ὀδυρμός.definition: lamentation, A.Pr.33; E.Ph.1071; Id.Tr.609; Pl.R.387d; ib.398d, al., cf. Call.Fr.1.7 P.: c. gen., lamentation for . . , Plu.Demetr.47

ὀδύρομαι.definition: mostly used in pres. and impf., Ep; c. acc. pers., Il.2.315; 24.714, cf. S.OC1439, Ant.693: less freq. c. acc. rei, mourned for it, i.e. for the want of it, Od.13.219; so 5.153, 13.379; Pl.R.329b; Isoc.4.169; D.18.41;…

Ὀδύσσεια.definition: the Odyssey, Hdt.4.29, Pl.R.393b, Arist.Rh.1406b12, Po.1449a1, al., AP7.377:—Adj. of or for the Odyssey, title of work by Hdn.Gr., Sch.Ar.Av.862

ὄζαινα.definition: a fetid polypus in the nose; a strong-smelling sea-polypus, also called and Call.Fr.38

ὀζαινίτης.definition: fem. smelling like an name of an Indian form of Plin.HN12.42

ὀζόομαι.definition: Pass., put forth branches or knots, Hp.Nat.Puer.22; Thphr.CP3.5.1

ὀζόστομος.definition: with foul breath, AP11.427 , M.Ant.5.28, Orib.Fr.24

ὄζω.definition: Dor. Theoc.1.149 : impf; freq. impers., there is a smell from it as of violets, Hdt.3.23; there is a sweet smell from the skin, Ar.Pl.1020; Cratin.Jun.1; there seemed to be a most foul smell from . . , Lys.6.1; no sce…

ὄθομαι.definition: only pres. and impf., take heed, Hom. only in Il., and always with neg.: abs., Il.15.107: c. inf., ib.166, cf. 182: with part. for inf., 5.403: c. gen. pers., regard, . . 1.181; A.R.3.94, cf. 1.1267

ὀθόνη.definition: fine linen, in Hom. always pl., fine linen; later, sails, AP12.53.8 , cf. 10.5 : sg., sail-cloth, sail, Luc.JTr.46, VH2.37

ὀθονιακός.definition: dealer in POxy.933.33; tax on cloth, Sammelb. 5941.3

ὀθόνιον.definition: Dim. of linen cloth, Hp.Acut.7; sail-cloth, D.47.20, Plb.5.89.2; so perh. in PPetr.1p.79

ὀθονιοπώλης.definition: linen-merchant, UPZ109.13 , v.l. in Dsc.5.134; = lintearius, Gloss

οἰακίζω.definition: Ion. steer: hence, govern, guide; metaph., Heraclit.64; Arist.EN1172a21:—Pass., D.S.18.59

οἰακονομέω.definition: steer, guide, govern, Ph.1.601: metaph., ib.419

οἴγω.definition: Hes.Op.819, etc.; later AP9.356 : fut. E.Cyc.502: aor. Il.24.457; but augm. forms usu. have in Ep. ; part. Il. : Ion. pf. Pass. Herod.4.55: the compd. or is much commoner, cf. also Il.6.89; ib.298; E.HF332; Id.Alc.547…

οἰδαλέος.definition: swollen, Archil.9.4; Nic.Al.210: in late Prose, Dsc.Eup.1.78, Aret.SD1.16, etc.: Comp. Alex. Trall.Febr.3

οἰδέω.definition: rarely Plu.2.734f: impf. Od.5.455; metaph., when affairs were in a ferment, Hdt.3.76, 127; metaph. from a boil or abscess, Pl.Grg.518e; Plu.Sol.19; also, of inflated style, Ar.Ra.940, cf. Plu.Cic.26

οἴδημα.definition: swelling, tumour, Hp.Aph.4.34, D.54.11, Plu.Cor.15; only of soft and painless tumours, acc. to Gal.17.801, 15.770, 17.31:—Dim. Hp.Fract.5; name of an eye-salve, Aët.7.118

οἴδησις.definition: swelling, fermenting, Pl.Ti.70c; puffiness, Phld.Vit.p.27 J.; of dropsy, Hippiatr.38

ὀϊζύω.definition: aor. wail, mourn; c. acc. rei, suffer, 14.89: abs., to be miserable or suffer, Od.4.152, 23.307. of pres. short in Hom., long in A.R.4.1324, 1374; in aor. always long.]

οἴζω.definition: cry lament, A.D.Adv.128.10, who also coins to expl

οἰηματίας.definition: self-conceited person, Ptol.Tetr.162, Hsch. s.v. Suid

οἴησις.definition: = opinion, notion; = self-conceit, Heraclit.46, E.Fr.643, Bion ap.D.L.4.50, Ph.1.53, al., Chor.inRh.Mus.49.512; Phld.Vit.p.29J

οἰησίσοφος.definition: wise in his own conceit, Ph.1.125, Procl.in Cra.p.67 P

οἰκειοποιέω.definition: appropriate, attach, cf cities, Sch. Philostr.Her.p.502 B.:—Med., make one's own, attach to oneself, Candid. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.55 B., Sch.Th.2.33; adopt, Ammon.Vit.Arist.p.10 W

οἰκειοπραγία.definition: minding one's own affairs, Pl.R.434c, Plot.1.2.7, Marin.Procl.24

οἰκειόφωνος.definition: by word of mouth : in Adv. Ctes.Fr.29.9

οἰκειόω.definition: make a person a kinsman, Th.3.65; c. acc. pers., make a person one's friend, Hdt.4.148, Pl.Lg.738d; reconcile, Phld.Rh.2.222 S., cf. Plu.Oth.2; D.H.9.44: abs., make friends, Aen.Tact.24.5:—Pass., to be made friendly, …

οἰκείωμα.definition: in pl., private or family affairs; affinity, Str.6.2.3

οἰκείωσις.definition: affinity, Ph.1.142, al.; attraction, affection , Diogenian.Epicur.4.55, Ph.1.256, Stoic.1.49, al., Asp.in EN44.27, cf. Hierocl.p.35 A.; Plot.4.4.44; propensity, Gal.5.456; opp. Plot.3.6.1, 3.8.8, al., Porph.Sent.18; b…

οἰκετεία.definition: household of slaves, Str.14.5.2; servitude, Aristeas14, al., J.AJ8.6.3

οἰκέτης.definition: household slave, A.Ch.737; also, = household, A.Ag.732 , Hdt.8.4, 106,142, S.Tr.908, X.Cyr.4.2.2: hence opp. Pl.Lg.763a, 777a, 853e; Stoic.3.86: but freq. synon. with Arist.Pol.1252b12, al., PLille 29.2 , IG5.1390.77 …

οἰκέω.definition: Ep. Hes.Th.330, Locr; colonize, settle in, Th.1.8, cf. 2.27, etc.; prob. in E.Fr.360.11; i.e. to be deported, POxy.1101.24 : in pf. Pass., to be settled in, occupy, Hdt.1.27; ib.142

οἴκημα.definition: room, chamber, Hdt.1.164, 179, 148, Th.1.134, 3.68, Lys.19.31, Pl.Thg.130d, Prt.315d, etc.; esp. bed-chamber, Hdt.1.9, 10, Pl.Smp.217d; dining-room, Heraclid.Cum.2

οἰκημάτιον.definition: Dim. of IG22.2496.11, PCair.Zen.507.29 , Arr.Epict.1.28.16, Plu.2.145b, PRyl.77.30 , X.Eph.2.10

οἴκησις.definition: the act of dwelling or inhabiting; management, administration, Pl.Min.321b

οἰκητήρ.definition: poet. for S.OC627, restored by Herm. for in A.Th.19

οἰκητήριον.definition: dwelling-place, habitation; Astrol., house, Thrasyll. in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.100.7

οἰκητής.definition: dweller, inhabitant, S.OT1450, Pl.Phd.111b : Locr. colonist, IG9.334.47; ib.9.517.5

οἰκίδιον.definition: Dim. of small house; tower on the back of an elephant, in pl., Plb.Fr.162B

οἰκίζω.definition: fut. Th.1.100, 6.23: aor. Ion; people with new settlers, colonize, Id.5.42, 7.143; v.l. in Th.1.8: c. gen. pers., . . having colonized it with . . . Id.6.4:—Med., we shall make ourselves a fenced home, E.Heracl.46, cf…

οἰκιήτης.definition: Ion.for Pherecyd. ap. D.L.1.122, Ant.Lib.41.2: Locr., Thess., Arc. IG9.334.44, 9.257, 5.262.16 ; St.Byz. s.v. EM698.11

οἰκίον.definition: in form Dim. of but in meaning not differing from it ; in early Gr. always pl., house, palace, Il.6.15, al.; abode of a deity, Od.12.4, Hes.Th.744; of the nether world, Il.20.64; of palaces containing several ranges o…

οἰκίσκος.definition: Dim. of small room or chamber; cage, Ar.Fr.405, cf. 441, Metag.5, Inscr.Délos 422.11 , Philostr.VS1.21.3

οἰκισμός.definition: = Sol.19.5; foundations of cities, Pl.Lg.708d, cf. Ephes.2.20

οἰκιστήρ.definition: poet. for Pi.O.7.30, al., Orac. ap. Hdt.4.155, Call.Ap.67, Abh.Berl.Akad.1925.21 ; cf

οἰκιστής.definition: colonizer, founder of a city, IG 12.15.30, Hdt.4.159, 6.38, Th.1.24, 3.92, 6.3, etc.; also of those who frame constitutions or charters for a city, Id.3.34, Pl.R.379a; = Lat. triumviri coloniae deducendae, App.BC1.24

οἰκιτιεύς.definition: Com. word for with play on Bion ap.Ath.4.162d

οἰκόβιος.definition: living at home, domestic, Sch.Pi.N.8.58 codd

οἰκογένεια.definition: certificate of origin of an; status of an PGnom.67

οἰκογενής.definition: born in the house, homebred, of slaves, Pl.Men.82b, Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39 xii 27, Plb.38.15.3, POxy.48.4 , etc.; GDI1842 , cf. IG9.1066 ; GDI1859, 1897, al.; also Ar.Pax789; Arist.HA558b20; Plu.2.480b: metaph., opp. ib.…

οἰκοδέγμων.definition: one who receives people into his house, Trag.Adesp.594

οἰκοδέκτωρ.definition: Astrol., a planet in whose domicile another planet happens to be, Vett.Val.186.15, Paul.Al.F.2, Rhetor. in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.206, PMich. in Class.Phil.22.13

οἰκοδεσπόζω.definition: of a planet, to be dominant, Ptol.Tetr.121

οἰκοδέσποινα.definition: mistress of a family, SIG985.52 , Phintys ap.Stob.4.23.61, Babr.10.5, Plu.2.613a

οἰκοδεσποσύνη.definition: household rule, CIG2987 , Keil-Premerstein Erster BerichtNo.170.13, Supp.Epigr.4.574

οἰκοδεσποτέω.definition: to be master of a house or head of a; Astrol., predominate, POxy.235.16 , PLond.1.130.163 , Plu.2.908c, Ptol.Tetr.39, Luc.Astr.20, Vett.Val.64.8, Iamb.Myst.9.5, etc.; cf. sq. II

οἰκοδεσπότης.definition: master or steward of a house; native ruler, opp. foreign emperor, J.Ap.2.11

οἰκοδεσπότησις.definition: Astrol., predominance of a planet, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.240

οἰκοδομέω.definition: fut. aor. (not in; generally, fashion, LXX3 Ki.6.36

οἰκοδομή.definition: = sq., Ev.Matt.24.1, Plu.Luc.39, CIG 4449 , al.: metaph., I Ep.Cor.3.9

οἰκοδόμημα.definition: building, structure, 136, Th.5.11, Antipho Soph.24, Pl.Grg.514b, etc

οἰκοδόμησις.definition: act or manner of building; = Id.Criti.117a, Lg.778e

οἰκόθετος.definition: laid up at home, i.e. one's own, Pi.Pae.1.4

οἰκοκερδής.definition: profitable to a house or family, Phryn.PSp.96 B

οἰκοκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., live under family rule, i.e. without civil bonds or laws, Eust.1618.20

οἰκονομέω.definition: manage as a house-steward, order, regulate; dispense, Pl.Phdr.256e; disburse, SIG667.20

οἰκονομία.definition: management of a household or family; generally, direction, regulation, Epicur.Ep.1p.29U.; esp. of a State, administration, Din.1.97; principles of government, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.338; Plb.1.4.3, al.; Phld.Rh.2.32 S.; Hdn…

οἰκονόμισσα.definition: perh. wife of or female official in the church, JHS24.283 , Papers of Amer. Sch. at Athens3p.216

οἰκονόμος.definition: one who manages a household, =; generally, manager, administrator, opp. Id.Pol.1314b7, etc.: hence

οἰκόπεδον.definition: site of a house, place on which a house; the house itself, building, Th.4.90, Pl.Lg.741c

οἰκοσιτία.definition: living at one's own expense, Poll.6.36

οἰκόσιτος.definition: taking one's meals at home; living in a house, of a mouse, opp. Babr.108.4; cf

οἰκοσκευή.definition: household utensils, PLond.5.1708.44 , PMasp.153.20 , Arc.103, Gloss.:—also gloss on Sch.Patm.D.27.10

οἰκοσκοπικόν.definition: observation of an omen at home, An.Ox.4.240

οἰκοσόος.definition: maintaining the house, of an economical wife, opp. Max.98: poet. Nonn.D.21.270

οἰκοτραφής.definition: homebred, Hellenistic for Moer.p.283 P., Gloss., v.l. in Poll.3.76

οἰκοτρίβαιος.definition: belonging to an Poll.3.76; corrupted into in Hsch

οἰκοτριβής.definition: ruining a house or family, Critias6.14

οἰκότριψ.definition: a slave born and bred in the house, Att. for , of a mouse , Babr.107.2; as a term of abuse, the slave E., Ar.Th.426; D.13.24; Ael.VH12.15: metaph., Phld.Acad.Ind.p.19M

οἰκότροφος.definition: house-bred, dub. in OGI765.19 ; living at home, dub. in D.Chr.6.11

οἰκουμένη.definition: inhabited region, v. A.I; the Roman world, i.e. the Emperor, OGI666.4, 668.5, POxy.1021.5 , CIG2581-2, 4416, Ev.Luc.2.1, Act.Ap.17.6, 24.5, Sammelb.176.2 , Gal.10.7, Luc.Macr.7

οἰκουρέω.definition: usu. in pres., watch or keep the house; keep at home, as women, S.OC343; Pl.R.451d, cf. D.59.86, Plu.Cam.11, Luc.Nigr.18; of persons who stay at home and avoid military service, Hermipp.45, Plu.Per.11, 12, etc

οἰκούρημα.definition: the watch or keeping of a house; keeping the house, staying at home, E.Heracl.700

οἰκουρία.definition: housekeeping and its cares, in pl; keeping-at-home, esp. of women, Plu.2.271e, Cor.35

οἰκούριος.definition: of or for housekeeping: hence; keeping within doors: toys to keep children within doors, to amuse them in their mother's absence, Hsch., Eust.1423.3; female house-mates, Pi.P.9.19

οἰκοφθορέω.definition: squander one's substance, Pl.Lg.929d, 959c:—Pass., lose one's fortune, be ruined, Hdt.5.29, cf. 8.142, 144; Id.1.196

οἰκοφθορία.definition: a squandering one's substance; seduction, Plu.2.12b

οἰκοφθόρος.definition: one who ruins a house, a prodigal; seducer, adulterer, PGrenf. 1.53.19 , Suid. s.v

οἰκοφυλακέω.definition: watch a house, of a dog, v.l. in Aesop.176 Chambry

οἰκτίζω.definition: Med. also, bewail, lament, E.IT486, cf.Hel.1053: abs., Din.1.110: c. acc. cogn., utter a wail, A.Eu.515 , cf. E.Tr.155

οἰκτιρμός.definition: pity, compassion, Pi.P.1.85: pl., compassionate feelings, mercies, Ep.Rom.12.1, Ep.Phil.2.1, al

οἰκτίρμων.definition: gen. merciful, Gorg.Pal.32, Theoc.15.75,AP7.359, LXXEx.34.6, al., Ev.Luc.6.36

οἰκτίρω.definition: impf. Stesich.18: fut. A.Fr.199.6 : aor. Il.11.814, A.Pr.354, al.; Ion. Hdt.3.52:-Pass., only pres. and impf., ibid., X.Oec.7.40, S.El.1412:-later forms : fut. Sch.Od.4.740, LXXEx.33.19, Ep.Rom.9.15, Lib.Descr.30.18: …

οἴκτιστος.definition: irreg. Sup. of most pitiable, lamentable, . . . Il.22.76; Od.11.412; Call.Aet.1.1.4; Od.12.258; A.R.2.782: neut. pl. as Adv., Od.22.472: also in late Prose, Onos.42.21, Luc.Anach.11. Adv. Phalar.Ep.96

οἰκωφελής.definition: beneficial to the house, only in Adv. D.C.56.7

οἰμάω.definition: only fut. and aor., swoop or pounce; abs., dart along, Orac. ap. Hdt.1.62

οἴμη.definition: = metaph., way of song, song, lay, Od.8.481; 22.347; . . 8.74; power of song, Anacreont.32.14; A.R.4.150; Call.Del.9; Lyc.11

οἰμωγή.definition: wailing, lamentation, Il.22.409; 24.696; 4.450, quoted by Ar.Pax1276; Hdt.3.66, cf. 8.99; . . A.Pers.426; S.Ph.190 ; Id.Aj.317; E.Heracl.833; Th.7.71; X.HG2.2.3; cf

οἴμωγμα.definition: cry of lamentation, wail, A.Th.1028, al., E.Ba.1112, al.: pl., A.Ag.1346, al

οἰμώζω.definition: Hom.Epigr.14.20, Tyrt.7, Ar.Ra.257, etc; in familiar Att., as a curse, plague take you ! Ar.Ach.1035; Id.Ra.257; Id.Pl.876; Id.Nu.217; Id.Pl.58, cf. Luc.Gall.23; Ar.Ra.178, cf. X.HG2.3.56, Men.Epit.428; Ar.Ach.840; Id…

οἰνανθάριον.definition: Dim. of sq., a compound ointment, Alex.Trall.7.3, Paul.Aeg.7.21

οἰνάνθη.definition: inflorescence of the grape-vine; Dropwort, Spiraea Filipendula, a plant with a smell like the vine, Cratin.98, Arist.HA549b33, Thphr.HP6.8.1, Dsc.3.120, Plin.HN21.65

οἰνάνθινος.definition: made of the wild-vine flower , Thphr.Od.27, Apollon. ap. Ath.15.689a, Gal.11.110; Dsc.1.46; Id.5.25

οἰνάρεος.definition: of vine leaves or twigs, Ibyc.1.6; Hp.Mul.2.195

οἰναρίζω.definition: strip off vine-leaves, as is done when the grapes are ripening, Ar.Pax1147, Phan.Hist.37

οἰνάριον.definition: Dim. of weak or bad wine; a little wine, Diocl.Fr.141, Epict.Ench.12, Sor.1.64, AP11.189

οἴναρον.definition: vine-leaf or tendril, X.Oec.19.18; vine, Alciphr.3.22

οἰνέλαιον.definition: wine mingled with oil, Dsc.4.150.7, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.11.11, Gal.13.404, Hippiatr.22, Simp.in Cat.230.10

οἰνήρυσις.definition: vessel for drawing wine, Ar.Ach.1067, Ph.1.390

οἰνίδιον.definition: Dim. of small wine, poor wine, Apollod. ap. D.L.10.11

οἰνίζω.definition: resemble wine, Thphr. ap; Med., procure wine by barter, buy wine, . . Il.7.472; 8.506, cf. 546: in later Prose, Max.Tyr.39.1; Luc.VH1.9

οἰνιστηρία.definition: cup used at this festival, Pamphil. ap. Ath.11.494f:—also Poll.6.22

οἰνοβαρείων.definition: = Od.9.374,10.555:—hence to be heavy or drunken with wine, Thgn.503

οἰνόγαλα.definition: milk mixed with wine, Hp.Mul.1.80 , Epid.7.82

οἰνοδόκος.definition: receiving or holding wine, Pi.I.6.40; AP6.33 : as Subst. c. gen., ib.257

οἰνοδοσία.definition: largess of wine, IGRom.3.833a.19; prescribing of wine, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.27.1

οἰνοδότης.definition: giver of wine, of Dionysus, E.HF682 ; of a physician, Gal.Thras.24, cf.IG14.666:— also of Asclepiades, Anon.Lond.24.30

οἰνοδόχος.definition: containing wine, ibid.,EM247.2: as Subst., cupbearer, LXXTo.1.22

οἰνοηθητής.definition: one who strains wine, Parmenio ap.Ath.13.608a

οἰνοθήρας.definition: a plant the root of which smells of wine or was used to flavour wine; but in the best Mss. of Thphr.HP9.19.1 it is as in Dsc.4.117 and Gal.12.89; called also Gal.l.c., and ibid., Aët.15.15; cf. onothuris, Plin. HN24.167

οἰνοκηκίς.definition: styptic made of oak-galls boiled in Gal.12.25

οἰνόκρεον.definition: meat preserved in vinegar, PSI9.1073 , PKlein.Form.773 , PGrenf.2.99.3 , etc

οἰνολογία.definition: a tax which was paidin wine, Ostr.711 , Ostr.Bodl.i144

οἰνομανής.definition: mad for or after wine, Ath.11.464e

οἰνόμελι.definition: honey mixed with wine, a kind of mead, Plb.12.2.7, Carnead. ap. D.L.4.64, Posidon.1 J., Mim.Oxy.413iii161, al., AP12.164 , Dsc.5.8, Gal.10.356, etc

οἰνομύρσινον.definition: wine in oil of myrtles, v.l. in Paul.Aeg.7.12.31

οἰνοπαραλημπτής.definition: = Lat. susceptor vinarius, POxy.1141.2 , PKlein.Form.1132 , etc

οἰνοπίπης.definition: gaping after wine, Com. word formed after cited by Sch. and Suid. from Ar.Th.393

οἰνοποσία.definition: drinking of wine, Hp.Acut.37, Arist.Pr.871a1 ; Ael.VH2.41, cf. CIG3028 , Supp.Epigr.4.598.9

οἰνοποτάζω.definition: drink wine, Il.20.84, Od.6.309, 20.262, Anacr.94.1, Phoc.11

οἰνοποτέω.definition: = foreg., LXXPr.24.72, Ath.11.460c, Erot. s.v. Orib.5.31.12: c. acc., Call.Aet.1.1.12

οἰνοπότης.definition: wine-bibber, Anacr.97, Call.Epigr.37, Plb.20.8.2, LXXPr.23.20, Ev.Matt.11.19:—fem. Anacr.162, Ar.Th.393

οἰνοπώλης.definition: wine-merchant, ib.21, Diph.3.6, PFay.63.8 , etc.:—fem. Sch.Ar.Pl.435, Lib.Decl.26.18

οἰνοφλυγέω.definition: to be drunken or drunk, LXXDe.21.20, Ph.1.361, Poll.6.21

οἰνοφλυγία.definition: drunkenness, X.Oec.1.22, Antiph.19, Arist.EN1114a27, Plb.2.19.4 , 1 Ep.Pet.4.3

οἰνόφλυξ.definition: given to drinking, drunken, Hp.Prorrh.2.2, X.Ap.19, Pl.Erx.405e, Arist.Po.1461a15

οἰνοφόρος.definition: holding wine, Critias6.2 D; Subst. , wine-jar, Poll.6.14: oenophorus Probus in Gramm.Lat.4.211 K

οἰνοφύλαξ.definition: an officer who had charge of the municipal wines, Michel 1226 , CIG3663A14 , JHS22.206 , Milet.3p.177 No. 33e5

οἰνόφυτος.definition: planted or grown with vines; Act., planting vines, Nonn.D.21.174

οἰνοχαρής.definition: merry with wine, IG14.2125; as a nickname, ib.3.1379

οἰνοχάρων.definition: Wine-Charon, Com. epith. of Philip of Macedon , because he put poison in his enemies' wine, and so sent them over the Styx; including an allusion to his being fond of wine , AP11.12

οἰνοχειριστής.definition: dispenser of wine, POxy.1752.1 , PSI3.191 , etc

οἰνοχοεύω.definition: Od.21.142; part. 1.143; inf; c. acc., she was pouring out nectar, 4.3; . . . . Il.1.598: metaph., Plu.Per.7; Dionys.Eleg.4.1:—Pass., Plu.2.349f

οἰνοχόη.definition: vessel for taking wine from the mixing-; a kind of sideboard to range the wine-cups on, Phryn.PSp.95 B

οἰνοχόημα.definition: a festival at which wine was offered, Ephor.80 J., Plu.Phoc.6, Polyaen.3.11.2

οἰνοχόος.definition: cupbearer, Il.2.128, Od.18.418, Hdt.3.34, E.Cyc.560, Pl.R.562d , X.HG7.1.38, Critias33 D.; Ion Eleg.2.2: dat. sg. contr. PTeb.122Intr

οἰνόχυτος.definition: of poured wine, draught of; Act., = Nonn.D.13.256,33.74, al

οἰνόω.definition: intoxicate, Critias6.28D; Pass., turn into wine, Nonn.D.11.517

οἰνών.definition: wine-cellar, X.HG6.2.6, IG22.1013.9, PSI4.396.5 ; wine-shop, Timae.60, cf. Gp.7.7.6

οἴνωσις.definition: drunkenness, not so bad as Stoic.3.179, cf. Dsc.5.6, Plu.2.503f, 645a, Gal.19.105: pl., D.L.7.183; Corn.ND30

οἰνώψ.definition: = of Dionysus, S.OT211 , prob. in E.Ba.236; f.l. in S.OC674

οἰοβουκόλος.definition: herdsman of one heifer, i.e. Io, A.Supp.304

οἰοβώτας.definition: feeding alone, prop. of cattle, metaph. of Ajax, = S.Aj.614

οἰόζωνος.definition: alone and girt up, i.e. lonely wayfarer, S.OT846

οἴομαι.definition: in Hom. always uncontr. (exc; impersonal, only Od.19.312, there comes a boding into my heart

Οἶον.definition: Oeum, name of two Attic demes; in the IG22.1926.127, Harp

οἰόομαι.definition: Pass., to be left alone, forsaken, Ep. Verb, only in aor., Il.6.1, 11.401; Q.S.6.527

οἰοπέδη.definition: perh. a woollen bandage for sore feet, AP7.401

οἰοπολέω.definition: roam alone, E.Cyc.74 : c. acc. loci, roam over, of shepherds, AP7.657

οἰοπόλος.definition: of places, lonely; tending sheep, Id.Dith.2.19; h.Merc.314; v.l. in Coluth.309; of the Hesperides, A.R.4.1322, cf. 1413; Coluth.15. in Sch.Il.13.473.)

οἰοχίτων.definition: with only a tunic on, lightly clad, Od.14.489, Nonn.D.8.16

ὀΐστευμα.definition: an arrow from the bow, Plu.2.225b

ὀϊστεύω.definition: shoot arrows, whom; trans., shoot with an arrow, AP5.57 ; Nonn.D.15.322

ὀϊστοδέγμων.definition: gen. holding arrows, i.e. a quiver, A.Pers.1020

οἰστράω.definition: or the former in Pl; intr., go mad, rage, of Io driven by the gadfly, in frenzy, frantically, A.Pr.836; of Menelaus, E.IA77; of the tunny when attacked by the , Arist.HA602a26, cf. 598a18: metaph., Pl.Phdr.251d, cf. R…

οἰστρηλασία.definition: mad passion, LXX4 Ma.2.4, Suid. s.v

οἰστρήλατος.definition: driven by a gadfly, A.Pr.580 , cf. E.Oxy.2078 Fr.1.15

οἴστρημα.definition: the smart of a gadfly's sting, metaph., S.OT1318; ravings of madness, AP6.51

οἴστρησις.definition: mad passion, Corp.Herm.13.4, cf. Ael.Fr.122, Gp.17.5.4

οἰστροβολέω.definition: strike with the sting, esp. of the dart of love, AP9.16

οἰστροδίνητος.definition: driven round and round by the gadfly, A.Pr.589

οἰστρομανής.definition: mad from the gadfly's sting: raging, Tim.Pers.90, Nonn.D.1.282

οἰστροπλάνεια.definition: causing the wanderings of madness, epith. of Hecate, PMag.Par.1.2868

οἰστροπλήξ.definition: stung by a gadfly, driven wild, of Io, A.Pr.681, S.El.5; of Bacchantes, E.Ba.1229

οἰσύϊνος.definition: of osier, of wickerwork, Od.5.256; Th.4.9; X.HG2.4.25; AP6.246; Opp.H.3.372

οἰσύπη.definition: also the grease extracted from sheep's wool , Hdt.4.187; Hp.Mul.2.195; used for medicinal purposes, Dsc. and Plin. ll.cc.: —freq. confused with

οἴφω.definition: Dor. = I, but only of human beings, Plu.Pyrrh.28, cf. IG12.536 , Leg.Gort.2.3; as if from in prov. Mimn.15 Diehl, Com.Adesp.36, Diogenian.2.2:—hence and fem. lewd, IG12.97 , Hsch., Eust.1597.29

οἰχνέω.definition: go, come, Il.5.790,15.640 (in Iterat; like to be gone, Id.Aj.564; Id.El.313

οἴχομαι.definition: impf. , the only; rarely in a general sense, go or come, without the idea of departure, and without a perfect sense, Il.1.53, cf. 5.495; more freq. go, go away, go off, Il.1.380, 13.38, 23.564, Od.17.104, al.: but usu…

οἰωνίζομαι.definition: generally, divine from omens, c. acc. et inf., X.HG ll. cc., LXXGe.44.5

οἰώνισμα.definition: omen from the flight or cries of birds, E.Ph.839, cf. LXX1 Ki.15.23, Je.14.14 , Hdn.1.14.2, D.C.37.24; = Salutis augurium, Id.51.20; a portent, monster, Gal.2.623

οἰωνιστήριον.definition: place for watching the flight of; omen or token, X.Ap.12

οἰωνιστής.definition: one who foretells from the flight and cries of birds, Il.2.858, 17.218, Hes.Sc.185; Il.13.70: in late Prose, Gal.9.833; = Lat. augur, D.H.10.57, D.C.37.27,al

οἰωνόβρωτος.definition: to be eaten of birds, Phld.Mort.33, Str.15.3.20 , LXX2 Ma.9.15, 3 Ma.6.34, Hsch., Suid

οἰωνόθροος.definition: of the cry of birds, the wailing cry of birds, A.Ag.56

οἰωνοπόλος.definition: one busied with the flight and cries of birds, an augur, Il.1.69,6.76, A.Supp.57 ; = Lat. augur, D.H.2.64,3.69: as Adj., Pi.Pae.4.30

οἰωνοσκοπεῖον.definition: place where auguries are taken, Paus.9.16.1

οἰωνόσκοπος.definition: = E.Supp.500, IG12.528 , Epigr.Gr.391 ; = Lat. augur, D.H.3.70, etc

ὀκέλλω.definition: trans. of seamen, run [a ship] aground or on shore, Hdt.l.c., Th.l.c.; of a wave, E.IT1379

ὀκλαδία.definition: Suid., perh. to be read in Cael. Aur.TP5.133

ὀκλαδίας.definition: folding-chair, camp-stool, IG12.282.119, Ar.Eq.1384,1386, Luc.Lex.6; Paus.1.27.1, Heraclid. Pont. ap.Ath.12.512c

ὀκλάζω.definition: metaph., sink, slacken, abate, Ph.1.199; Gal.11.172; Musae.325; of the wind, Hld.5.23, cf. Adam.Vent.37; ib.7; AP5.250

ὄκλασις.definition: crouching with bent hams, squatting, Hp.Art.82, Luc.Salt.41

ὄκλασμα.definition: a Persian dance in which the dancer squatted from time to time, Ar.Fr.344b

ὀκνέω.definition: Ep. Il.5.255: impf. 20.155: fut; of shame or fear , I shrink from being called, fear to be called, S.Ph.93, cf. Th.5.61, Lys.Fr.23; shrink from naming, hesitate to name, D.2.19, cf. Pl.Grg.462e; . . D.18.103, cf. 24.7…

ὄκνος.definition: shrinking, hesitation; personified, as title of picture by Polygnotus, Paus.10.29.2, Plin.HN35.137, cf. D.S.1.97

ὀκριάζω.definition: to be rough or angry, S.Fr.1075

ὀκριάομαι.definition: Pass., to be made rough or jagged: metaph., they grew furiously angry with each other, Od.18.33; enraged, Lyc.545

ὀκτάβλωμος.definition: consisting of eight pieces, an obscure conjunction of epithets, Hes.Op.442, cf. Philostr.Im.2.26

ὀκταδάκτυλος.definition: eight fingers long or broad, Clearch.73, PCair.Zen.483 :— older Att. Ar.Lys.109, Supp.Epigr.3.137 iii 11 , IG22.1627.123, and so in Ion., Hp.Steril.221

ὀκτάδραχμος.definition: worth eight drachmae, Epigr. ap; privileged to pay only eight drachmae as poll-tax, Sammelb. 7440.6, 32

ὀκτάεδρος.definition: of a solid figure, eight-sided, Gal.5.668: Subst. octahedron, Arist.Cael.307a16, Ti.Locr.98d, Euc.11Def.26, Placit.2.6.5

ὀκτάειδος.definition: containing eight ingredients, v.l. in Paul.Aeg.3.78

ὀκταετηρίς.definition: cycle of eight years, used at Athens before Meton's time for bringing the lunar and solar years together, 3 months being intercalated to complete the sum of 2,922 days, Eudox.Ars13.12, Str.7.5.5, Gem.8.27 sqq., Placit…

ὀκταετία.definition: = Theo Sm.p.173 H., Procl.Par.Ptol.285; but in Ptol.Tetr.205

ὀκτάκωλος.definition: of eight lines, Sch. Ar.Ach.565, Heph.Poëm.4

ὀκταμερής.definition: of or in eight parts, D.L.7.110

ὀκτάμετρος.definition: of eight measures : octameter, Sch.Heph.p.132 C

ὀκταμηνιαῖος.definition: of eight months, D.S.14.38; POxy.1627.9 ; eight months old, Ar.Byz.Epit.77.18

ὀκτάμηνος.definition: eight months old, in the eighth month, Hp.Alim.42, X.Cyn.7.6, Arist.HA545a29, etc.; of eight months' duration, IG11.199A13 ; as fem., X. l.c., Hp.Epid.2.3.17; PCair.Zen.327.77 ; but Arist.HA583b33

ὀκταπάλαιστος.definition: eight palms wide or long, Ael.Tact.12: so Ascl.Tact.5.1

ὀκτάπλεθρος.definition: eight plethra long or large, D.H.4.61

ὀκταπόδης.definition: eight feet long, Hes.Op.425; eight-footed, Nic.Th.605

ὀκτάπους.definition: gen. eight-footed; Subst., Octopus vulgaris, Alex.Trall.7.1

ὀκτάρριζος.definition: with eight roots, of a stag's horns, with eight points, AP6.110

ὀκτάρρυμος.definition: of chariots, with eight poles, or rather, so constructed as to be drawn by eight pairs of horses or oxen, X.Cyr.6.1.52

ὀκτάσημος.definition: in Prosody, of eight times, Sch.A.Th.103. Adv. in the eight-time measure, of the dochmius , Sch.A.Th.128

ὀκτασκελής.definition: eight-legged, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.21.1, cf. Gal.18.774

ὀκτάστυλος.definition: with eight columns in front, of temples, Vitr.3.2.7

ὀκτάσφαιρος.definition: system of eight spheres, Phlp.in Ph.599.10, al.: as neut., Simp.in Cael.435.4

ὀκτάτευχος.definition: the volume containing the first eight books of the Old Testament, Phot.Bibl.pp.7,128 B.: title of work by Ostanes, Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10

ὀκτάτονος.definition: eight-stretched, the eight arms of the octopus, AP9.14

ὀκτάτροπος.definition: the first eight of the Vett.Val.334.20

ὀκτάχορδος.definition: with eight strings or notes, Plu.2.1029c; Aristox.Harm.p.96 M., Theo Sm.p.49 H.: octachord, Nicom.Harm.11, POxy.667.24

ὀκτάχρονος.definition: composed of eight time-units, Procl.in Prm.p.990S

ὀκτώ.definition: Boeot. IG7.3193.6, 9 , Heraclean Tab.Heracl.1.34, Elean Schwyzer 419.4 : indecl., eight, Il.2.313, etc. : prov. in reference to the eight spheres, Timoth. ap. Theo Sm.p.105 H

ὀκτώβιβλος.definition: a work in eight volumes, Gal.7.311

ὀκτωκαιδεκάδραχμος.definition: at the price of eighteen drachmae, D.42.20

ὀκτωκαιδεκαετηρίς.definition: period of eighteen years, Ptol.Alm.4.3, al

ὀκτωκαιδεκαπλάσιος.definition: eighteen-fold, Aristarch.Sam.7, Placit.2.31.2, Plu.2.925c, Procl.Hyp.4.107:—also gen. Archim.Aren.1.9

ὀκτωκαιδέκατος.definition: eighteenth, on the eighteenth day, Od.5.279, 24.65; Plb.1.56.2, etc. ; Boeot. Schwyzer 485.39

ὀκτώμηνος.definition: = EM767.34:—also Ph.1.29, Sch.Arat.455; born in the eighth month, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.47

ὀκτώφορος.definition: borne by eight, octophorus lectica or octophorus alone, a litter carried by eight, Cic.Verr.5.11.27, QF2.8.2; octǎphorus, Mart.6.84

ὀλβίζω.definition: fut. E.Hel.228: aor. S.Fr.646.1, etc. :—Pass. :—make happy, E.Ph.1689, Hel.l.c.; deem or pronounce happy, A.Ag.928, S.OT1529, etc. :—Pass., to be or be deemed happy, . . Id.Fr.942; E.IA51; Id.Tr.1253

ὀλβιογάστωρ.definition: whose happiness is in his belly, a belly-god, Amphis10

ὀλβιοδώτης.definition: bestower of bliss, Orph.H.34.2:—fem. ib.40.2, etc

ὀλβιότυφος.definition: happy in his own conceit, said of Archytas, Bion ap.D.L.4.52

ὀλβοδοτήρ.definition: giver of wealth, cj. Pierson in Them.Or.13.178b

ὀλβοδότης.definition: giver of bliss or wealth, E.Ba.573 , Epic.Alex. Adesp.9vi6 , Epigr.Gr.978.10 , IG42.424, 425 , Orph.H.68.8:—fem. ib.27.9

ὀλεθριάω.definition: to be on the point of death, Archig. ap. Aët.9.40

ὀλέθριος.definition: c.gen., bringing ruin on his friends, A.Ag.1156; c. dat., as Subst., name of a fluid, Philum.Ven.12.4

ὄλεθρος.definition: ruin, destruction, death; that which causes destruction, pest, plague, Hes.Th.326; contemptuously of persons, Hdt.3.142; Ar.Lys.325; Eup.376, cf. Men.533.13; of Philip, D.9.31; a pestilent scribe, of Aeschines, Id.18.…

ὀλέκω.definition: impf. without augm. Il.11.150; Iterat. 19.135:—pres. Phot., Suid.:—ruin, destroy, kill, Hom. always in last sense, and mostly of men, Il.18.172, cf. 15.249, Theoc.22.108, etc. ; but in Od.22.305, of birds which prey o…

ὀλεσισιαλοκάλαμος.definition: made of spittle- wasting reed, epith. of the flute in Pratin.Lyr.1.12

ὀλετήρ.definition: destroyer, murderer, Il.18.114, Alcm.43, Nic.Th.735, etc. :—fem. Batr.117, Euph.3, AP11.424

ὀλίγαιμος.definition: scant of blood, Hp.Oss.13, Arist.PA651b9, al. ; ib.692a21

ὀλιγανάφορος.definition: quick in rising, of a zodiacal sign, Vett. Val.136.7, Heph.Astr.2.11, Ps.-Ptol.Centil.52

ὀλιγανδρέω.definition: to be scant of men, D.S.15.63, Plu.Publ.11, D.C.49.1

ὀλιγανδρία.definition: scantiness of men, Str.14.1.10, Plu.2.413f, Philostr.VA3.30

ὀλιγανθρωπέω.definition: = Theagen.17; are short of their number of priests, PGnom.85 :—Med., J.AJ11.5.8

ὀλιγαρκέω.definition: to be contented with little, Aesop.384, dub. cj. in Gp.14.7.25

ὀλιγαρκής.definition: contented with little, Luc.Tim.57; = sq., ib.54

ὀλιγαρχέω.definition: to be a member of an oligarchy, Arist.Pol.1300a8:—Pass., to be governed by the few, be under an oligarchy, Th.5.31, 8.63,76, Pl.R.552b, al

ὀλιγαῦλαξ.definition: having but little arable land, AP6.226 Brunck)

ὀλιγεκτέω.definition: have little, Theol.Ar.29:—Subst. in pl., Nicom.Ar.1.14

ὀλιγήμερος.definition: of or lasting a few days; lasting a short time, prob. in Antyll. ap. Orib.10.23.16

ὀλιγήριος.definition: = foreg., a small tombstone, AP7.656 : or perh. compd. of

ὀλιγησίπυος.definition: with little corn, or with a small bread-basket, opp. ib.288 , 300

ὀλιγογονία.definition: production of few offspring, opp. Pl.Prt.321b

ὀλιγόγονος.definition: producing few offspring, opp. Hdt.3.108, Arist.HA558b28; unprolific, Vett.Val.5.25; of plants, Thphr.HP8.4.4: Comp. Arist.HA570b32

ὀλιγογράμματος.definition: composed of few letters, opp. Phld.Po.Herc.994.34

ὀλιγοδάπανος.definition: consuming or spending little, Suid. s.v

ὀλιγοδεής.definition: wanting little, Posidon.59J., M.Ant.5.5; 'cheaper' popularity, Plb.16.20.4: Sup., Ph.1.116

ὀλιγοδίαιτος.definition: living on little, Cephisodor. ap. Caryst.7

ὀλιγοδρανέω.definition: in Ep. pres. part. able to do little, feeble, powerless, Il.15.246, 16.843, 22.337 : also in late Prose, Ph.1.460, cf. 2.573, Jul.Caes.331b: pres. ind. Iamb.Myst.2.8

ὀλιγοδρανής.definition: of little might, feeble, Ar.Av.686, Luc.Trag.324

ὀλιγοδρομέω.definition: of the moon, to be retarded, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.102.7b

ὀλιγοθερμία.definition: possession of little heat, Mich.in PN132.22

ὀλιγόθερμος.definition: having little heat, of cold-blooded animals, Arist.PA652b25, GA718b37, al. ; of the spleen, Id.PA670b7, etc

ὀλιγοθυμέω.definition: to be of little courage, Eust.159.17

ὀλιγοκάλαμος.definition: with few reeds or stalks, Thphr.CP4.11.4

ὀλιγόκαρπος.definition: bearing little fruit, Thphr.CP2.11.10, D.H.1.37, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.7.4

ὀλιγοκίνητος.definition: little-moving, Porph. ap. Stob.2.8.41. Phlp.in Cat.166.9

ὀλιγομετρία.definition: in Prosody, the having few feet, Eust.353.39

ὀλιγόξυλος.definition: with little wood, shrubby, AP6.226 ; bearing little timber, Str.Chr.12.7

ὀλιγόπιστος.definition: of little faith, Ev.Matt.8.26, al., Sext.Sent. 6

ὀλιγοπόλιος.definition: with thin grey hair, Hsch. s.v

ὀλιγοποσία.definition: moderation in drinking, Aret.CD1.4, Luc.Par.16; but Aret.CD1.2

ὀλιγοπότης.definition: one who drinks little, Ath.10.419a, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.27.13

ὀλιγοπράγμων.definition: gen. averse to business, retiring, opp. ibid

ὀλιγόπυρος.definition: with few grains of wheat, Thphr.CP4.11.4

ὀλιγόσαρκος.definition: with little flesh, Luc.Abd.29, Gal.14.45, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.18.7

ὀλιγοσιτία.definition: small eating, moderation in food, Arist.Pol.1272a22,Pr.863b24, Thphr.Lass.17, Sor.1.65, etc

ὀλιγόσιτος.definition: eating little or moderately, Pherecr.1, Phryn.Com.23

ὀλιγόσπορος.definition: = foreg., of persons, Vett.Val.14.23; of a part of the zodiac. Heph.Astr.1.1

ὀλιγοστιχία.definition: the consisting of few lines, AP4.2.6

ὀλιγόστιχος.definition: consisting of few lines, Call.Aet.Oxy.2079.9, D.L.7.165

ὀλιγοσώματος.definition: of small body or bulk, Comp. Sch.Pl. ap.Plot.de Pulcr.p.536

ὀλιγότης.definition: opp. in all senses; fewness, Pl.Lg.678c, Arist.Metaph.984a10,al., LXXPs.101.23, Plu.Alex.20; fewness of rulers, Arist.Pol.1279b27

ὀλιγοτιμάω.definition: quote less than the true price, IG5.1421.14

ὀλιγοτοκία.definition: the bringing forth of few, ib.771b6

ὀλιγοτροφία.definition: little nourishment, Gal.6.209, Sor.1.65, Alex. Trall.Febr.3

ὀλιγότροφος.definition: giving little nourishment; Act., taking little nourishment, Arist.PA682a21, Pr.898b21; abstemious, of athletes in training, dub. in Delph.3.474

ὀλιγόϋπνος.definition: taking little or short sleep, App.Hisp.71 , Gal.10.538

ὀλιγοφόρος.definition: that can bear but little, of weak wine, that will bear but little water, Hp.Acut.56, Gal.6.807, cf. Sch.Ar.Pl.854

ὀλιγόφρων.definition: gen. of small understanding, Ph.2.70, al., Plu.2.504b, Poll.4.14. Adv. ib.15

ὀλιγόφωνος.definition: with little tone, prob. gloss on Aristid.Quint.1.20

ὀλιγοχρήματος.definition: of or with little money, Ph.1.287, al

ὀλιγοχρονέω.definition: take a short time to rise, Ptol.Tetr.132, Heph.Astr.2.11

ὀλιγοχρόνιος.definition: within a short time, Hp.Prog.7. Adv. Gal.18.243, Iamb.Protr.20

ὀλιγοχρονιότης.definition: shortness of time, Thphr.CP2.12.1, Ptol.Tetr.10, Heph.Astr.2.11; shortness of life, Ptol.Tetr.115, Vett.Val.147.3, Paul.Al.H.2

ὀλιγόχρυσος.definition: having little gold, poor in gold, Poll.3.109

ὀλιγόχυλος.definition: with little juice, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.120e, Dsc.2.182

ὀλιγοψυχέω.definition: to be faint, Isoc.19.39; become discouraged, PPetr.2p.135 , LXXNu.21.4, al., EM395.31

ὀλιγόω.definition: lessen, diminish, LXXHb.3.12; ib.Pr.10.27; his soul was grieved, ib.Jd.10.16,al

ὀλιγωρέω.definition: aor. I written IG12.53.5; later c. acc., neglect, PAvrom.1.25 : c. inf., intermit, neglect to do something, Gal.6.243

ὀλιγωρία.definition: Ion. an esteeming lightly; neglect of duty, negligence, Decret. ap. D.18.74; Eun.Hist.p.257 D

ὀλίγωρος.definition: little-caring, lightly-esteeming; of things, scornful, . . Nicom.Com.1.2

ὀλιζόω.definition: make less, diminish, Orac. ap. Eus.PE5.22:—Pass., Hsch

ὁλίζω.definition: make into a single whole, Olymp.inPhd.p.86 N

ὀλισθάνω.definition: slip or glide along, Pl.Cra.427b; Theoc.25.230; causal, sprain by slipping, Philostr.V A3.39, cf. Gym.14

ὀλίσθημα.definition: luxation, Hp.Fract.14, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.9.16, Gal.19.460, etc

ὀλίσθησις.definition: slipping and falling, ib.611a, 731f: hence, dislocation, Hp.Fract.42, Art.74

ὀλισθογνωμονέω.definition: make a slip in judgement, Luc.Lex.19

ὁλκαῖον.definition: stern-post of a ship, A.R.1.1314, Antioch. ap.Poll.6.100; cf

ὁλκαῖος.definition: drawn along, towed, of a ship; as Subst. Ion. tail, because it is trailed along, Nic.Th.123, 225, A.R.4.1614

ὁλκάς.definition: ship which is towed: hence, trading; of stones, conveyed to the place of building, IG11.199A79

ὁλκή.definition: drawing, trailing, dragging, e. g. of; inhalation , Hp.Mul.1.55; drawing in of the breath, Arist.Spir.482a15; suction of blood by the cupping-bowl, Anon.in Rh.170.8

ὅλκιμος.definition: capable of being drawn out, ductile; Act., drawing well, of a cupping instrument, Paul.Aeg.6.41

ὁλκός.definition: drawing to oneself, attractive; trailing, Hld.10.30. Adv. Comp. slowly, Id.3.5

ὄλλυμι.definition: destroy, make an end of, and of living beings, kill, Il.8.498, cf. Od.23.319; . . Pi.P.3.41; A.Th.1061 ; S.Ant.751; E.Andr.856 ; Orac. ap.Arist.Fr.544; also, of doing away with evil, A.Ag.1017

ὁλμίσκος.definition: Dim. of II, socket of the hinge of; tooth-socket, Ruf.Onom.55; the hollows of the molar teeth, Poll.2.93

ὁλμοκοπέω.definition: bray in a mortar, Heras ap.Gal.13.1043,al., Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.70, Alex.Trall.12, Aët.4.30

ὁλμοκόπος.definition: one who brays in a mortar, Anon.in Gal

ὁλόβηρον.definition: genuine purple dye, Procop.Arc.25: as Adj., holovera vestimenta, dyed purple through and through, Cod.Just.11.9.4

ὁλογράμματος.definition: with all its letters, written at full length, title of work by Menecrates, Gal.13.503. Adv. Id.14.44

ὁλογραφία.definition: will written entirely in the handwriting of the testator, Gloss

ὁλόγραφος.definition: written in full, in Adv; written entirely in the same hand, PSI3.223.6 , PGrenf.2.89.6

ὁλόγυρος.definition: entirely round, all round, in Adv. HeroGeom.4.13

ὁλοήμερος.definition: working the whole day, BGU14iii 2; lasting the whole day, in Adv. Tz.ad Hes.Op.566

ὁλοθούριον.definition: holothurium, a kind of zoöphyte, Arist.HA487b15, PA681a17, Plin.HN9.154

ὀλοθρεύω.definition: destroy, v.l. for in LXXEx.12.23, al., Ph.1.73 , Ep.Hebr.11.28; cf. destroyer, I Ep.Cor.10.10:—fem. gloss on Hsch

ὁλοκάλαμος.definition: stake made of a single reed, BGU1529.10

ὁλοκαρπόομαι.definition: Pass., to be offered as a whole burnt- offering, LXXSi.45.14,4 Ma.18.11

ὁλόκαρπος.definition: brought as a whole offering, Ph.1.668

ὁλοκάρπωσις.definition: presentation of such an offering, ib.Ge.8.20, al

ὁλοκαυτέω.definition: bring a burnt-offering, offer whole, X.An.7.8.4: impf. ib.5:—Pass., J.AJ3.9.1:—more usu. v.l. in X.Cyr.8.3.24; J.AJ1.13.1, etc

ὁλόκαυτος.definition: burnt whole, Call.Fr.1.49 P; in full flame, opp. Gal.18.225

ὁλοκαύτωσις.definition: sacrifice of a burnt-offering, LXXEx.29.25, al., J.AJ3.9.1: but IG42.97.2, al. ; cf

ὁλοκληρέω.definition: to be in good health, POxy.1158.3 , PMag.Par.1.136, etc

ὁλοκληρία.definition: completeness or soundness in all parts, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.33, Plu.2.1041f: abs., Act.Ap.3.16, Plu.2.1063f, Demetr.Eloc.3, SIG1142 , POxy.123.6

ὁλόκληρος.definition: complete, entire, perfect, opp. Arist.HA585b36; uncastrated, Pl.Com.174.9; Anaxandr.39.10, cf. Men.233, Luc.Asin.33; Pl.Ti.44c; Diog.Oen.39; . . . . , . . perfect, complete, Pl.Phdr.250c; Id.Lg.759c; Luc.Philops.8; al…

ὁλόκνημος.definition: with the whole shin, a ham containing the whole leg, Pherecr.108.13

ὁλόκυρος.definition: Pontic for Dsc.3.158, Apollod. ap. Ath.15.681d

ὁλοκωνῖτις.definition: earth-almond, Cyperus esculentus, Hp.Mul.1.78, cf. Gal.19.126; also

ὁλόλευκος.definition: all white, Antiph.186.3; Philetaer.20; Plu.Arat.53; Paus.8.17.3; albino, Heph.Astr.1.1

ὀλολυγή.definition: any loud cry, esp. of women invoking a god, Il.6.301, cf. h.Ven.19 , Ar.Lys.240; Hdt.4.189; Ar.Av.222; of the alarm given in the attack on Plataea, Th.2.4.—Mostly in good sense, sts. even opp. to a wailing cry, E.Med.…

ὀλόλυγμα.definition: loud cry, mostly of joy, E.Heracl.782 ; in honour of C., AP6.173

ὀλολυγμός.definition: loud cry, mostly of joy, in honour of the gods, . . A.Th.268; Id.Ag.28, cf. 595, E.Or.1137, LXXZe.1.10, PMag.Lond.121.323: pl., Epicur.Fr.143,419; song of triumph, . . A.Ch.387 ; rarely of lamentation, AP7.182

ὀλολυγών.definition: croaking of the male frog; in Theoc.7.139, Arat.948, an unknown animal, evidently named from its note : some take it for a small owl, others for a singing bird, others again for the tree-frog ; cf. Eub.104, Thphr.Sign…

ὀλολύζω.definition: Od.22.411, etc. : fut. E.El.691, later LXXIs.16.7, Am.8.3: aor. Ep. :—cry with a loud voice, in Hom. esp. of women crying aloud to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving, Od.4.767, cf. h.Ap.445; at a sacrifice, Od.3.450; …

ὁλομέλεια.definition: Pythag. name for six, Anatolius ap.Theol.Ar.36: Ion

ὁλομελής.definition: whole of limb, not dismembered, Diph.34.2; Posidon.9 J.,IG12.515.49 ; alone, Str.15.3.19; uniform, Dsc.1.26

ὁλομερής.definition: in entire parts, in large or whole pieces, D.S.5.28, Dsc.5.75. Adv. Arist. ap. D.L.5.28

ὁλόμεστος.definition: solid, without marrow, of bones, Pall.in Hp.12.286 C

ὁλονύκτιος.definition: the whole night through: neut. as Adv., Sch.Lyc.815

ὁλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be constituted a whole, Dam.Pr.276, cf. EM821.37

ὁλοποιέω.definition: make into a whole, Simp.in Ph.636.38, Dam.Pr.159

ὁλόπτερος.definition: with whole wings, a generic name of insects such as bees, wasps, etc., opp. Arist.APo.96b39, cf. PA692b13,IA709b30,713a4

ὀλόπτω.definition: pluck out, tear out; strip off, Nic.Th.595

ὁλόπυρος.definition: of unground wheat, esp. of wheat boiled

ὁλόρριζος.definition: with the entire root, Thphr.HP3.18.5: metaph., LXXJb.4.7

ὁλοσηρικοπράτης.definition: in Lat. form holosericoprata, silk-mercer, Champollion-Figeac Chartes Latines1 vi 14, al

ὁλοσίδηρος.definition: all iron, IG22.1481 , cf. Antiph.216, IG11.145.37 , Plu.Cam.40; soldiers wearing coats of mail, = Lat. clibanarii, Lyd.Mag.1.46

ὁλοσπάς.definition: drunk all at one draught, S.Fr.1076 ap.Phot

ὁλοστήμων.definition: gen. consisting all of warp- threads, Poll.7.32

ὁλόστομος.definition: tempered all through, of an iron ring, PMag.Par.1.2961; Cyran.6

ὁλόσφαλτος.definition: quite defective, marg. gloss in cod. of AP6.269

ὁλοσφύρατος.definition: Ion. made of solid beaten metal, opp. cast, hollow, AP11.174 , cf. LXXSi.50.9, Plin.HN33.82, Hsch.s.vv. condemned by Phryn.180

ὁλοσφύριον.definition: piece of beaten metal, Ammon.Diff.p.41 V

ὁλόσφυρος.definition: = Herm.in Phdr.p.82A., cf. Hsch.; interpol. in Phryn.180, v.l. in Artem.2.5

ὁλοσχέρεια.definition: general survey or estimate, Str.2.1.24; lumpiness, solidity, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.34

ὁλοσχερής.definition: whole, entire, complete, Hp.Alim.26; in large pieces, opp. Aristo Stoic.1.89, cf. Chrysipp. ib.2.158

ὁλόσχιστος.definition: cut out in one piece, Pl.Plt.279d, 280c

ὁλόσχοινος.definition: club-rush, Scirpus Holoschoenus, Thphr.HP4.12.1,9.12.1, Dsc.4.52: used in wicker- work, sts., like flax. soaked for use , sts. without soaking , Ael.NA12.43: hence prov., stop Philip's mouth with an unsoaked rush , i.…

ὁλοσώματος.definition: of or with the whole body, Hld.4.17; full-length portrait, JHS9.248

ὁλοτελής.definition: quite complete, 1 Ep.Thess.5.23, Placit.5.21.2, Vett.Val.247.8; IG 7.2713.45 . Adv. gloss on Suid., cf. Nech. ap. Vett.Val.155.3, Peripl.M.Rubr.30, Aq.De.13.16

ὁλότης.definition: wholeness, entireness, Arist.Metaph.1023b36, S.E.M.10.52, Dam.Pr.158, Procl.Inst.67, etc

ὁλότμητος.definition: cut in large pieces, Phryn.PSp.94 B

ὀλοφρονέω.definition: for to be crafty, deceitful, Wiener Sitzb.132.24

ὁλοφυής.definition: grown as a whole, consisting all of one piece, Arist.PA693a25; having the nature of a whole, Dam.Pr.271, cf. 51; cf

ὀλοφύρομαι.definition: used mostly in pres.: but fut; intr., lament, wail, moan, freq. in pres. part., Il.5.871, al. : with an Adv., 24.328; Od.10.409; 22.447, cf. Hdt.2.141, Democr.107a; Th.6.78: abs., Pl.R.329a

ὀλόφυρσις.definition: = Th.1.143; lamentations for . . , Id.2.51, cf. J.BJ Prooem.4, Philostr.VA4.45

ὁλόφωνος.definition: full-voiced, or vox et praeterea nihil, of the cock, Cratin.259

ὁλόχαλκος.definition: all of brass or copper, Sch.E.Ph.120

ὁλοχρόνιος.definition: all the year through, Hdn.Epim.186. Adv. Tz.ad Hes.Op.31

ὁλόχροος.definition: contr. all of one colour, Arist.GA785b19

ὁλόχρυσος.definition: of solid gold, Antiph.224.5, Call.Iamb.1.130, Callix.2, Plu.2.852b: metaph., Phld.Rh.1.190 S

ὁλοψυχέω.definition: prob. misspelling of or to be faint-hearted, PLond.ined.2132

ὁλόψυχος.definition: dub.sens. in Phld.D.3.Fr.19 ; with his whole soul, Eust.1901.43. Adv. Suid. s.v

Ὀλυμπία.definition: Olympia, district round Pisa; the Olympic games, or games in honour of Olympian Zeus, Hdt.1.59, etc. : mostly without the Art., Id.8.26; having won at the Olympic games, Id.6.36; ; Plu.2.179d: also with the Art., X.HG…

Ὀλυμπίας ἄνεμος.definition: the WNW. wind, elsewh. or Arist.Mete.363b24, Mu.394b26, Lyd.Mens.4.119

Ὀλυμπιάς.definition: = fem. of Olympian; olive-crowns of the Olympic games, Pi.N.1.17

Ὀλυμπιεῖον.definition: or temple of Olympian; his festival, IG22.1496.82 , 2.1291.6 :—later ib.3.127 , al

Ὀλυμπιοδρόμος.definition: running at the Olympic games, B.3.3

Ὀλυμπιονίκη.definition: victory at Olympia, Id.4.17, Antipho Soph.49

Ὀλυμπιόνικος.definition: victorious in the Olympic games, ib.5.21, al

ὀλυνθάζω.definition: impregnate the female palm-tree with the pollen of the male , Thphr.HP2.8.4, CP2.9.15.—Used by analogy, cf

ὄλυρα.definition: rice-wheat, a cultural variety of 2, Thphr.HP8.9.2, Diocl.Fr.113, Dsc.2.91

ὀλύρινος.definition: of wheat mixed with PSI5.537.6 ; made of Gal.6.504

ὁμαδέω.definition: make a noise or din, of a number of people all speaking at once. in Od. always of the suitors, 1.365, al. , cf. A.R.2.638, etc

ὅμαδος.definition: noise, din, esp. of the confused voices of; noisy throng or mob of warriors, 7.307, 15.689, 17.380: metaph., Pl.R.364e

ὀμάζω.definition: growl, of bears and panthers, Zenod. ap. Valck.Animadv. ad Ammon.p.174

ὁμαίμιος.definition: related by blood, Pi.N.6.16; cf. sq

ὅμαιμος.definition: of the same blood, related by blood; mostly as Subst., or brother or sister, Id.Th.681, Eu.605, etc. ; S.El.12; ib.325, cf. BMus.Inscr.1036.6 : Boeot. gen. pl. Corinn.Supp.2.68

ὁμαίμων.definition: as Subst., brother or sister, Id.Aj.1312, OC1275

ὁμαιχμέω.definition: fight on the same side with one, Opp.H.5.160

ὁμαιχμία.definition: Ion. union for battle, defensive alliance, league, Th.1.18, App.Gall.15; form a league with one, against one, Id.7.145: pl., Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

ὅμαιχμος.definition: fighting together: as Subst., ally, Th.3.58

ὁμαλής.definition: level, even, of the ground; equable, even, Arist.Ph.228b28, cf. 223b21, al. ; of music, Id.Pr.918a12; v.l. for in Epicur.Ep.2 pp.49,53 U

ὁμαλίζω.definition: X.Oec.18.5, Arist. : fut; level, equalize, Arist.Pol.1266b30, cf. 1267b5:—Pass., ib.1270a39; ib.1265a40; Isoc.5.40, cf. 6.65

ὁμάλιξις.definition: levelling of sand for athletic contests, BCH23.566 , Milet.7.60

ὁμαλισμός.definition: levelling, LXXBa.5.7, cf; one must read without a rise of pitch, of enclitics, Sch.A.Ag.937, Sch.Ar.Pl.414; D.T.630.1

ὁμαλιστήρ.definition: instrument for levelling, strickle, in pl., Gloss

ὁμαλότης.definition: evenness of surface; equability, equilibrium, Pl.Ti.57e; lose equilibrium, ib.58e

ὁμαλύνω.definition: = I.1, Hp.Haem.5, cf; bring the body to an even temperature, Id.Mete.381a20, cf. Metaph.1032b19

ὁμαρτέω.definition: accompany, Il.24.438; could not keep pace, keep up with the ship, Od.13.87

ὅμαστος.definition: united in one city , prob. l. in Herod.2.7

ὁμαῦλαξ.definition: Dor. with adjoining lands, A.R.2.396, AP7.402

ὁμαυλία.definition: a dwelling together, wedded unions, A.Ch.599

ὅμαυλος.definition: living together, companion; playing together on the flute, sounding together in concert, Id.OT187

ὀμβρέω.definition: trans., rain or shower down upon, Ph.1.402; Id.2.397, cf. Nonn.D.2.33

ὄμβριος.definition: rainy, of rain, rain-water, Xenoph.30.4, SIG56.29 , Hdt.2.25, Hp.Aër.7, etc. ; Pi.O.10.3; S.OC1502; Ar.Nu.288; as sender of rain, Lyc.160, cf. Str.15.1.69, Plu.2.158e

ὁμείρομαι.definition: or desire, long for, v.l. for in best codd. of LXXJb.3.21 and I Ep.Thess.2.8, cf. Sm.Ps.62.2, Hsch., Phot.; CIG4000.7

ὀμείχω.definition: make water, Hes.Op.727, Pythag. ap. D.L.8.17: aor. Hippon.55A
