ὁμευνέτης.definition: = E.Med.953,Ion894: in late Prose, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.203:— fem. S.Aj.501, Epigr.Gr.781.8 ; and Lyc.372; cf. Hsch

ὅμευνος.definition: sleeping together, partner of the bed, both of the man and woman, Maiist.3, AP7.735 , Nic.Th.131, Man.3.148

ὁμηγυρής.definition: Dor. v.l. for in Il.1.57,7.415, Pi.P.11.8

ὁμήγυρις.definition: Dor. assembly, meeting, esp. of the gods, Il.20.142, h.Ap.187, cf. h.Merc.332, Hellanic.54 J.; Pi.I.7.46; any assembly, company, A.Ch.10; E.Hipp.1180; . . A.Ag.4

ὁμήθεια.definition: poet. a living together, in pl., Opp.C.4.2, Man.6.188

ὁμηλικία.definition: Ion. sameness of age (so; of one person, = but he is of the same age with myself, Od.3.49; 22.209, cf. 6.23; of two persons, Il.13.485

Ὁμήρειον.definition: shrine of Homer in Smyrna, Str.14.1.37; at Delos, Inscr.Délos443 Bb 147

Ὁμήρειος.definition: Homeric, Hdt.5.67, Ar.Fr.222; also Alex.Aet.5.6; the Homeric phrase, Hp.Mochl.5; = II, Pl.Tht.179e. Adv. Ael.NA15.16

ὁμηρεύω.definition: to be or serve as a hostage; take as a hostage, E.Rh.434:—Med., give hostages, Aen.Tact.10.23

Ὁμηρίδης.definition: mostly in pl. the; imitators or admirers of Homer, Pl.R.599e, Phdr.252b, Ion530d, Isoc.10.65

Ὁμηρίζω.definition: imitate Homer, use Homeric phrases; act scenes from Homer, Artem.4.2

Ὁμηριστής.definition: rhapsode, Aristocl.Hist.10; actor of Homeric scenes, Artem.4.2; mentioned in Ach. Tat.3.20; cf. II

Ὁμηροκέντρων.definition: patchwork of Homeric tags, AP9.381 tit., etc

Ὁμηρομαντεῖον.definition: divination by means of verses of Homer, PMag. Lond.121.148a

Ὁμηρομάστιξ.definition: scourge of Homer, i.e.the Grammarian Zoïlus, from his spiteful criticisms on the Homeric poems, Gal.10.19, Suid.: in pl., generally, of Homeric critics, Eust.1702.44

Ὁμηροπάτης.definition: one who tramples on Homer, epith. of Xenophanes in Timo60.1 as quoted by D.L.9.18, but codd. S.E.P.1.224, which may be nom. masc., perverter of Homer, or gen. of the Homeric fiction, as expld. by S.E

ὁμιλέω.definition: Aeol. 3sg. pres. Alc.61.29 Lobel, to; abs., joining in company, 4.684; throng about the corpse, Il.16.641, cf. Od.24.19

ὁμίλημα.definition: of a person, bad company, E.Fr.219, cf. Luc.Am.25

ὁμιλητής.definition: disciple, scholar, X.Mem.1.2.12.48; one who has experience, of Heracles, Max.Tyr.3.7

ὁμιλία.definition: Ion. intercourse, company; sexual intercourse, Hdt.1.182, X.Smp.8.22, Mem.3.11.14, etc. ; E.Hel.1400; Arist.HA582a26; or Id.Pol.1272a24, 1269b29

ὀμιχλοειδής.definition: mist-like, Epicur.Ep.2p.54U.:—also misty, Ti.Locr.99c, Thphr.CP5.10.3, Plb.3.84.1, Gal.15.382, etc

ὀμματογράφος.definition: painting or staining the eyes, Ion Trag.25

ὀμματοστερής.definition: Act., depriving of eyes, heat that robs plants of their eyes or buds, A.Eu.940

ὀμματόω.definition: furnish with eyes; give sight to, Zos. Alch.p.117 B

ὄμνυμι.definition: swear to a thing, affirm or confirm by oath; folld. by fut. inf., swear that one will . . , Il.21.373, etc., cf. S.Ph.623,941 : freq. with Att. preceding the inf., . . Il.1.76, cf. 10.321, Lys.31.1, X.HG5.3.26, etc. :…

ὁμόβιος.definition: living together. Alciphr.1.12; sharing the same life, Olymp.in Phd.p.190 N

ὁμοβλαστέω.definition: shoot or bud at the same time, prob. for in Thphr.CP1.11.1

ὁμοβλαστής.definition: sprouting at the same time, ib.5.5.4

ὁμόβωμος.definition: = foreg., IG2.1442; of Demeter and Kore, Hsch

ὁμόγαμος.definition: married to the same wife: Amphitryon; of persons who have married sisters, Id.Ph.137

ὁμογάστριος.definition: from the same womb, born of the same mother, uterine, Il.24.47; 21.95; BGU405.5 ; Man.6.118; Hld.7.5

ὁμογένεια.definition: community of origin, Str.16.4.27; of plants, community of genus, Dsc.1Prooem.3

ὁμογενής.definition: of the same race or family; in Arist., of the same genus, in regard to animals, congeners, GA715a23, al. : generally, of the same kind or general character, Cat.5b19, al., Epicur.Ep.1p.14U., Ti.Locr.99d; opp. Demetr. …

ὁμογλωσσέω.definition: Att. speak the same tongue, D.C.41.58

ὁμόγλωσσος.definition: Att. speaking the same tongue, Hdt.8.144, Phld.Po.2.72; with one, Hdt.1.57,171, X.Cyr.1.1.5, etc

ὁμόγνητος.definition: = brother or sister, Man.6.117, Nonn.D.37.192: fem. Orph.A.1215: as Adj., Nonn.D.5.197

ὁμόγνιος.definition: of the same race, brother or sister

ὁμογνωμονέω.definition: to be of one mind, agree, Th.2.97; Philos., have the same judgements, Plot.4.7.5

ὁμογνωμοσύνη.definition: agreement in opinion, J.Ap.2.37, Iamb. ap. Stob.2.33.15

ὁμογνώμων.definition: gen. of one mind, like-minded, with one, Th.8.92, Lys.28.17, X.HG2.3.15, etc. ; bring to one's own opinion, Id.Cyr.2.2.24,5.5.46, Lac.8.1; IG14.952.28 . Adv. Lycurg.97

ὁμόγονος.definition: born at the same time with, Dam.Pr.387

ὁμόγραμμος.definition: of or with the same letters, Luc.Herm.40

ὁμογραφέω.definition: write in the same manner, Eust.1960.56

ὁμοδαίμων.definition: gen. sharing the same Olymp.in Phd.p.190 N

ὁμόδαις.definition: companion at table, Choerob.in Theod.1.187, 210 H

ὁμοδημέω.definition: to be of the same people with, Plu.2.823b

ὁμοδημία.definition: a living with others, agreement, Iamb.VP6.32

ὁμόδημος.definition: Dor. of the same people or race, Pi.O.9.44; with one, Id.I.1.30

ὁμοδίαιτα.definition: living in a common establishment, PLond.ined.2231

ὁμοδίαιτος.definition: living or eating with others, D.H.6.52, Nic.Dam.4J., Luc.Demon.5, Gal.6.598; Ph.2.32, al.; Luc.Abd.5; common to the generality, Id.Hist.Conscr.16

ὁμόδιφρος.definition: driving in the same chariot, Nonn.D.21.195

ὁμοδογματέω.definition: hold the same opinions, M.Ant.9.3: abs., metaph., Id.11.8

ὁμοδογματία.definition: agreement in opinion, common principle, Stoic.3.27

ὁμοδοξέω.definition: to be of the same opinion, agree perfectly, Pl.Phd.83d: abs., c. acc. et inf., Id.R.442d; Thphr.Sens.70, Plb.1.41.5

ὁμοδοξία.definition: agreement in opinion, unanimity, Pl.R.433c; opp. Arist.EN1167a23: pl., Pl.Plt.310e

ὁμόδοξος.definition: of the same opinion, Vit.Philonid.p.8 C., Luc.Eun.2, Porph.Abst.3.8, Simp.in Ph.1144.30; belonging to the same school, of the Epicureans, IG22.1099.24

ὁμόδουλος.definition: fellow-slave, E.Hec.60; metaph., of persons in love with the same woman, AP12.81

ὁμοδρομέω.definition: run on the same course with, Ti.Locr.97a, cf. Alcid.Soph.7, cf. Max.232, PMich. in Class.Phil.22.11: abs., keep pace, Plu.2.1143f

ὁμόδρομος.definition: running the same course with, Pl.Epin.987b, cf. Plu.2.1029b: c. gen., Nonn.D.1.250: abs., ib.48.318. Adv. Tz.H.10.537

ὁμοδυναμέω.definition: to be of the same power, Paul.Al.E.1, Procl.Par.Ptol.39

ὁμοεθνέω.definition: to be of the same people or race, D.S.15.39

ὁμοεθνής.definition: of the same people or race, Hdt.1.91; generally, of the same kind, Arist.EN1155a19; Ael.NA13.3

ὁμοεθνία.definition: lit., descent from the same people or race: then, connexion and sympathy of parts, Hp.Loc.Hom.1, Mul.2.174

ὁμοειδής.definition: of the same species or kind, whether in; of like form, Plb.34.11.17; homogeneous, Arist.Ph.188a13 , Metaph.1014a30. Adv. Phld.Rh.2.244 S., M.Ant.9.35

ὁμοερκής.definition: within the same house or prison, Sol. ap. Poll.6.156, Din.Fr.84 S.; of pillars in mines, like AB286:—also Phot

ὁμόζηλος.definition: of like zeal, Ph.2.458, Nonn.D.37.261; cultivating the same literary style, Anach. ap. S.E.M.7.56

ὁμοζυγέω.definition: to be yoked together, of a four-in-hand of dolphins, Philostr.Im.2.18: c. acc., not to keep the oars together, Hld.2.2

ὁμοζυγία.definition: a being yoked together: in Rhet., mutual affinity, of rhythms, D.H.Comp.18 ; rhythmical correspondence, ib.25

ὁμόζυγος.definition: yoked together, Plu.2.1008d; in the same row, Ascl.Tact.2.4

ὁμόζυξ.definition: = foreg., Pl.Phdr.256a; the female, An.Par.1.29; their fellows, Protarch. ap. Arist.Ph.197b11: metaph., Him.Or.5.13

ὁμοζώϊα.definition: living together, Olymp.in Alc.p.215 C., Procl.in Prm.p.538S

ὁμόζωνος.definition: houses of the same heavenly body, Vett.Val.269.9, Paul.Al.E.3, Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.124:—whence Paul.Al. l.c.; ibid., Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.122

ὁμοήθεια.definition: agreement of habits, Nic.Dam.139 J., Poll.3.62, Philostr.VA2.11

ὁμοθάλαμος.definition: living in the same house, c. gen., Pi.P.11.2

ὁμοθαμνέω.definition: grow up with the plant, M.Ant.11.8

ὁμόθριξ.definition: gen. with the same sort of hair, f.l. for Sophr.52 cj. for in Lyc.340)

ὁμοιάζω.definition: to be like, interpol. in; trans., compare, liken, Diom.p.365 K

ὁμοίεδρος.definition: having a similar abode, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ὁμοίιος.definition: Ep. Adj. of uncertain meaning, perh. distressing , Il.4.315, cf. h.Ven.244; Od.3.236; Il.4.444; 9.440, 13.358, 15.670, al. shd. be restored.)

ὁμοιογένεια.definition: likeness of race or kind, D.H.3.15

ὁμοιογενής.definition: akin, of like kind, Arist.GA715b9, Placit.4.19.2; D.H.Pomp.3. Adv. An.Ox.4.273

ὁμοιογονία.definition: generation of like offspring, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

ὁμοιόγραφος.definition: written alike, A.D.Conj.258.14; Subst., one who writes like another, a forger, Vett.Val.74.19

ὁμοιοειδής.definition: of like form, species or kind, Isoc.15.178, Arist.Cael.276b5,308b8 , Epicur.Ep.1p.25U. ; POxy.465.226

ὁμοιοκάταρκτος.definition: having a similar beginning, of words : neut. pl., of the rhetorical figure in which such words are used, prob. in Phld.Rh.1.162 S

ὁμοιοκλινής.definition: of like slope: hence, in the same latitude, of Byzantium and Sinope, Sch.Iamb.Comm.Math.14p.102F

ὁμοιολεπτομερής.definition: consisting of equally fine parts, Sch.Ar.Nu.230

ὁμοιόλογος.definition: having a common definition, Porph.in Cat.69.7

ὁμοιομέρεια.definition: a having like parts, similarity of composition, Epicur.Nat.14.6, al. ; esp. of the doctrine of Anaxagoras , nunc et Anaxagorae scrutemur homoeomerian Lucr.1.830; rerum h. ib.834: pl., in concrete sense, of the in this…

ὁμοιομερής.definition: having parts like each other and the whole, Arist.Cael.302b3, Metaph.984a14,988a28 ; Thphr.CP5.2.1; Epicur.Ep.1p.13U.; Simp.in Ph.27.5, cf. Gal.10.48,al

ὁμοιόμορφος.definition: of like form, Epicur.Ep.1p.12U., Alex.Aphr.in Sens.24.19

ὁμοιόνομος.definition: of like laws, Phint. ap. Stob.4.23.61a

ὁμοιοπάθεια.definition: sympathetic emotion; likeness in condition, homogeneousness, D.S.13.24 , cf. Str.1.1.9

ὁμοιοπαθέω.definition: have similar feelings or affections; of things, to be subject to the same laws, to be homogeneous, Str.1.1.9: Medic., to be affected in sympathy, Gal.8.756

ὁμοιοπαθής.definition: having like feelings or passions, Pl.R.409b, Act.Ap.14.15; affected in the same way, Pl.Ti.45c, Thphr.HP5.7.2; Agatharch.47, cf. 32

ὁμοιόπτωτος.definition: with a similar inflexion, in a like; Astrol., corresponding, Vett.Val.19.10

ὁμοιόρρυσμος.definition: Ion. for foreg., Hp.Anat.1, Pempel. ap. Stob.4.25.52

ὁμοιόσκευος.definition: in like dress or array, Str.17.3.7

ὁμοιόστομος.definition: with both fronts facing the same way, Ascl.Tact.10.22, 11.3, Ael.Tact.37.5, Arr.Tact.29.4. Adv. Ascl.Tact.11.4

ὁμοιοσύστατος.definition: similarly constituted, of physical bodies, Ptol.Harm.1.3

ὁμοιοσχημονέω.definition: to be like in form, Arist.Pr.866b34

ὁμοιοσχήμων.definition: gen. of like form, Democr. ap. Placit.4.19.3, Arist.APr.27b11, Thphr.HP4.2.4, Epicur.Ep.1 p.9U., Id.Nat.Herc.1420.3, D.H.Comp.26, Ptol.Tetr.104, etc. Adv. Arist.EE1217b35. is prob. in Corn.ND17, Phlp.in Mete.20.29; in…

ὁμοιοταχής.definition: moving with equal velocity, Sch.Arat.19. Adv. Arist.Mu.392a14

ὁμοιοτέλευτος.definition: ending alike: the like ending of two or more clauses or verses, Id.Rh.1410b1, Phld.Rh.1.162 S., D.S.12.53 : Demetr.Eloc.26; end a sentence with S.E.M.2.57

ὁμοιότης.definition: likeness, resemblance, Democr.164, Pl.Phd.109a, al. : pl., ib.82a, Sph.231a; mode of passing life like themselves, Id.Tht.177a; correspond to . . , Id.R.555a; so ib.576c; equally, Id.Ti.75d: c. dat., resemblance to . …

ὁμοιότονος.definition: of like tone or accent, D.H.Comp.12. Adv. Eust.1400.19

ὁμοιότροπος.definition: of like manners and life, Th.3.10; conformable, having similar effects, of medicines, Hp.Acut.23

ὁμοιόχρονος.definition: of equal or like duration: in Prosody, of equal length, D.H.Comp.12

ὁμοιόχροος.definition: contr. like- coloured, Phld.D.3.8 , Plot.2.8.1, Alex. Aphr.de An.146.11, Hippiatr.55

ὁμοιόχωρος.definition: belonging to a similar place, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ὁμοιόω.definition: liken, compare, in Med., Hdt.1.123:—later in Act., Ev.Matt.11.16; BSA29.35

ὁμοίωμα.definition: likeness, image, Pl.Phdr.250a, Arist.Rh.1356a31 , Epicur.Ep.1p.10U., Nat.11.6: pl., Pl.Phdr.250b, Sph.266d, al. ; in accordance with the practice in similar cases, by analogy, OGI669.52

ὁμοίωσις.definition: a being made like, Pl.Tht.176b; likeness, resemblance, Thphr.Lap.41; opp. Pl.R.454c; Ep.Jac.3.9, cf. LXXGe.1.26

ὁμοιωτής.definition: one who likens, = condemned by Poll.7.126

ὁμοκαρπέω.definition: bear fruit at the same time, Thphr.CP1.11.1

ὁμοκατάληκτος.definition: ending alike, of numbers, Iamb.in Nic.p.17 P., al.; cf

ὁμόκεντρος.definition: concentric with; at the same cardinal point, Vett.Val.60.14, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.136

ὁμοκίνητος.definition: moved at the same time, Sch.E.Ph.328

ὁμοκλάω.definition: Ep. impf. 3pl. and 3sg. : aor. Hom. , S.El.712; Ion. Iterat. :—Ep. Verb, call or shout to, c. dat., either to encourage, Il.15.658: once in Trag., S.El.712; or , to upbraid, threaten, Il.5.439, etc. ; 6.54, etc. ; 18.…

ὁμοκλή.definition: in later Ep., onset, attack, Nic.Th.311; of Sirius, Opp.H.1.152; of fire, ib.4.14, cf. Q.S.6.614, al., Man.2.374

ὁμόκληρος.definition: Dor. having an equal share; esp. of an inheritance, coheir, Pi.O.2.49, N.9.5

ὁμοκλήτειρα.definition: fem. of sq., as Adj., Lyc.1337

ὁμόκλητος.definition: called by the same name, Nic.Th.882, Hsch

ὁμόκλινος.definition: reclining on the same couch, at table, Hdt.9.16

ὁμόκτιτος.definition: lit. built together: hence, joint, common, Opp.H.4.352

ὁμοκωμήτης.definition: member of the same village- community, PThead.17.7 , PSI1.43.2

ὁμόλεκτρος.definition: sharing the same bed, E.Or.508; but of Tyndareos, as husband of Leda, ib.476: Subst., wife, AP7.295 , IG12.307 , Ath.Mitt.49.117

ὁμολεχής.definition: = foreg., v. II :—also Apollon.Lex.s.v. Sch.Th.7.78, and Sch.Pi.P.8.9

ὁμολογέω.definition: S.Ph.980 , Hdt. and; agree with, say the same thing as, c. dat., Hdt.1.23, cf. 171, 2.4; Id.4.154

ὁμολόγημα.definition: that which is agreed upon, taken; convention, compact, Arist.Rh.Al.1422a2, cf. 1424a10; in commerce, agreement or contract, POxy.237iv6 , etc

ὁμολογία.definition: assent, admission, concession, Isoc.11.44, cf. Pl.Grg.461b, al.; by my admission, Id.Prt.350e; Id.Tht.169e; argue from premises agreed upon or granted, Arist.Top.110a33

ὁμόλογος.definition: agreeing, of one mind; of persons, confessing guilt, Mitteis Chr.31 iii 12 ; BGU372 i 32

ὁμομήτριος.definition: born of the same mother, Hdt.1.92, 6.38, Pl.Prt.315a, etc. :—Dor. fem. Ar.Ach.790, cf. Nu.1372; Lys.32.4

ὁμόναος.definition: having a common temple, IG42.41.2 , Hsch. s.v

ὁμονοέω.definition: to be of one mind, agree, opp; c. dat., live in harmony with, And.1.108; Pl.R.352a; to be of one mind with him about . . , Id.Alc.1.126c, cf. Isoc.4.85; Arist.EN1167a29: metaph., Diog.Trag.1.11; Lys.2.43; of drugs, Ga…

ὁμόνοια.definition: oneness of mind, unanimity, concord; Pythag. name for 3 and for 9, Theol.Ar.16, 57

ὁμόνομος.definition: under the same laws; feeding together, Ael.NA7.17

ὁμόνοος.definition: contr. of one mind, united, Democr.255, Poll.6.155. Adv. X.Cyr.6.4.15, Ages.1.37, D.L.4.22

ὁμοούσιος.definition: consubstantial, Plot.4.4.28, 4.7.10, Porph.Abst.1.19, Iamb.Myst.3.21, Syrian.in Metaph.129.3, Simp.in Ph.44.3, etc

ὁμοπάθεια.definition: common affection or quality of two things, sympathy with one, Arist.Fr.101, cf. Plot.4.2.1, al

ὁμοπαθέω.definition: to have the same experience as, Id.4.9.1; Id.4.9.2, cf. Porph.Sent.32: metaph., of a vowel, to be reconciled, Plu.2.737f

ὁμοπαθής.definition: of the same feelings or affections, sympathetic, Apollod.Com.8, cf. Arist.EN1161a26; affected in the same way as others by pain and pleasure, Pl.R.464d; Max.Tyr.39.5; Id.15.1

ὁμοπάτριος.definition: but A.Pr.558 :—by the same father, Hdt.5.25, cf. Antipho1.1, Lys.19.22, Pl.Lg.774e, etc.; A. l.c.; Is.11.2, cf. Supp.Epigr.2.822 :—also Pl.Lg.924e, Is.11.1

ὁμοπληθής.definition: Math., of classes or series containing the same number of individuals or terms, terms with the same coefficient, Dioph.1 Def.10

ὁμοπλοέω.definition: sail together or in company, Plb.1.25.1

ὁμόπλοος.definition: contr. sailing together or in company with, Tryph.265; consort, AP7.635

ὁμοπλωτήρ.definition: one who sails in company, Opp.H.1.208

ὁμόπολις.definition: from or of the same city or state, Plu.2.276b, etc. : poet. S.Ant.733

ὁμόπολος.definition: of spheres or circles, having the same poles, Procl.in Ti.3.148 D.; Id.Hyp.2.1

ὁμόπτερος.definition: of or with the same plumage; metaph., of like feather, closely resembling, A.Ch.174, cf. E.El.530; consort-ships , A.Pers.559 ; i.e. the two brothers, Eteocles and Polynices, E.Ph.328

ὄμοργμα.definition: that which is wiped off, a spot, AB 432

ὀμόργνυμι.definition: wipe, aor. Act. opt. Nic.Th.558; cf. —Med., were drying their tears, Od.11.527, cf. 530; Il.18.124; Pythag. ap. D.L.8.17

ὁμορέω.definition: Ion. (also PLond.ined.2850.26 (ii; cohabit, have intercourse with, of a woman, Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19. .)

ὁμόρησις.definition: neighbourhood, juxtaposition, in Ion. form Epicur.Ep.1 p.20 U., Nat.22 G.: Astrol. v.l. of planets, prob. in Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.159, 8.107, 114, Porph.in Ptol.189

ὁμόριος.definition: Ion. = Call.Fr.185, A.R.2.379, D.P.649, etc.; for Plb.2.39.6, v

ὁμορροέω.definition: Astrol., of signs of the zodiac, rise together with, SerapioinCat.Cod.Astr.8.226

ὁμορροθέω.definition: flow together, Hp.Mul.1.17; row together; metaph., agree, consent, S.Ant.536, Fr.489 ; agree with . . , E.Or.530; Ael.NA6.32

ὁμόρροθος.definition: prop. rowing together : hence, side by side, Theoc.Ep.3.5:—also AP7.374

ὁμόρρυθμος.definition: Ion. of the same form, like, ibid

ὁμοσίπυος.definition: sharing the same meal-tub, messmate, Charond. ap.Arist.Pol.1252b14

ὁμοσιτέω.definition: eat with, take one's meals with, of women, Hdt.1.146

ὁμόσκευος.definition: equipped in the same way, Th.2.96,3.95; f.l. for X.Cyr. ap.D.H.Rh.8.11

ὁμοσκηνία.definition: living in the same tent, v.l. in X.Cyr.2.1.26

ὁμόσκηνος.definition: one living in the same tent, messmate; Adj., Max.Tyr.6.4; living with, J.AJ3.8.10

ὁμοσκηνόω.definition: live in the same tent, X.Cyr.2.1.25

ὁμοσπονδέω.definition: join one in a treaty, Poll.1.34, Phryn.PSp.95 B

ὁμόσπονδος.definition: sharing in the drink-offering; bound by treaty to, LXX3 Ma.3.7

ὁμόσπορος.definition: sown together : hence, sprung from the; a wife common to two , S.OT260; also of Oedipus, having the same wife with his father, ib.460

ὁμοστεγέω.definition: to be housed under the same roof, SIG1180.6

ὁμόστοιχος.definition: in the same line or rank with, Thphr.CP6.6.3, Jul.Or.5.163c, Dam.Pr.312; v.l. for in Plu.2.503d

ὁμόστολος.definition: in company with, attendant; generally, similar, A.Supp.496

ὁμόσφυρος.definition: walking in company, Hsch., Suid; sister, Hsch.; brother, EM625.31

ὁμοσχημονέω.definition: to be of the same form, cj. in Democr. ap. Thphr.Sens.50

ὁμοσχήμων.definition: gen. of the same shape, Thphr.HP4.2.4 , Sch.Il.23.65

ὁμοταγής.definition: ranged in the same row or line; coordinate with, Jul.Or.4.144d, cf. Heliod.in EN59.13, Iamb.Comm.Math.14, Procl.Inst.21,108, Dam.Pr.37. Adv. ib.119

ὁμοταχής.definition: of the same velocity, Arist.Cael.289b9, Ph.237a1, 249a8, etc. Adv. ib.236b35, Procl.Hyp.3.45, Simp.in Ph.992.24

ὁμοτελής.definition: paying the same taxes, Poll.3.56, Hsch.; SIG581.62

ὁμοτέρμων.definition: gen. having the same borders, marching with another, Pl.Lg.842e, cf. D.H.1.9,26, al.; Nic.Fr.5, cf. Scyl.22; Ath.14.625f

ὁμότεχνος.definition: practising the same art, with one; as Subst., fellow-workman, Hdt.2.89, Pl.Prt.328a, Xenarch.7.15; Pl.Chrm.171c, cf. D.22.58, Aristaenet.1.19; Alex.173.7: as title applied to the good physician, Hp.Praec.7

ὁμοτιμία.definition: sameness of value or honour, Luc.DMort.15.1

ὁμότιμος.definition: equally valued or honoured, held; equal in degree, Gal.10.745. Adv. Id.2.653, al.; Id.10.606, cf.Ascl.in Metaph.226.32, Steph.in Gal.1.270 D.: c. dat., . . no less than . . , Gal.9.385

ὁμότιτθος.definition: bred by the same nurse, Din.Fr.89.24 S., Phot

ὁμότοιχος.definition: having one common wall, contiguous; metaph., A.Ag.1004 ; Antiph.295; Plu.2.503d

ὁμοτονέω.definition: have the same tension, Ph.Bel.61.18; have the same pitch with, Nicom.Harm.12; have the same accent, A.D.Synt.51.24, al

ὁμότονος.definition: having the same tension, with equal; having the same pitch, in Music, Nicom.Harm.11.5; Gaud.Harm.21: neut. sg. between and Pl.Phlb.17c

ὁμοτράπεζος.definition: eating at the same table with , Hdt.9.16; Pl.Euthphr.4c; messmates, Persian name for certain of the chief courtiers, X.Cyr.7.1.30; cf

ὁμοτριβέω.definition: in part., fully polished stones fitting closely together, IG7.3073.164

ὁμοτροπία.definition: sameness of character or habits, D.H.4.28

ὁμότροπος.definition: of the same habits or life; of like fashion, Hdt.8.144; . . Id.2.49, cf. Aen.Tact.19, al. Adv. in the same manner, Id.3.3, Arist.SE183b6

ὁμότροφος.definition: reared or bred together with; abs., feeding together, having the same diet, Pl.Phd.83d

ὁμοτροχάω.definition: run in company or together, v.l. in Od.15.451 ; . . Man.6.527

ὁμοτυπία.definition: sameness of form, Philox.Gramm. ap. EM234.55

ὁμότυπος.definition: identical in tenor, PFlor.50.116 , PLips.28.23 , etc

ὁμουρέω.definition: Ion. for etc.; but Att. for , Hsch

ὁμόφθογγος.definition: sounding or giving tongue together, Nonn.D.1.157, etc

ὁμοφλεγής.definition: burning together or at once, ib.6.220

ὁμόφοιτος.definition: going by the side of, Pi.N.8.33 , Nonn.D.5.122, etc

ὁμοφράδμων.definition: gen. of the same mind, Lyr.Adesp.138.4

ὁμοφρονέω.definition: pf. Phld.Mus.p.86 K.:—to be of the same mind, have the same thoughts, Od.9.456; . . , in unity of purposes, 6.183; being all of one mind, Hdt.9.2; opp. Id.7.229; of conspirators, X.HG7.5.7, Arist.Ath.14.3; also a war …

ὁμοφροσύνη.definition: = unity of mind and feeling, Od.6.181, cf. Orph.A.353: pl., Od.15.198, A.R.2.716: also in Ion. and later Prose, Democr.186, D.H.9.45, Ocell.4.6, etc

ὁμόφρων.definition: = agreeing, united, Il.22.263, cf. Hes.Th.60, Thgn.81; Pi.O.7.6; Ar.Av.632 . Adv. Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.33; poet. IG9.235.6

ὁμοφυής.definition: of the same growth, age, or nature, Pl.Phd.86b, R.458c; with one, ib.439e; of hands and feet, Aret.SD2.12. Adv. Procl.in Prm.p.625 S

ὁμοφυΐα.definition: sameness of growth, age, or nature, Prisc. Lyd.27.19

ὁμοφυλία.definition: sameness of race or tribe, Str.1.2.34, Plu.2.975f

ὁμόφυλος.definition: of the same race or stock, akin (wider; generally, of the same breed or kind, Philol.6; X.Cyr.1.6.39; ib.8.7.20, cf. Arist.Mu.396b10; homogeneous matter, Id.Cael.307b1, cf. GC329b28

ὁμοφωνέω.definition: speak the same language with; sound together or in unison, D.C.41.58: c. dat., sound like, A.D.Pron.7.25, al.; chimes in with . . , Arist.EN1102b28; agree, Them.Or.21.258b; S.E.P.2.32

ὁμοφωνία.definition: in Music, unison; community of language, D.H.1.29; Ph.1.405

ὁμόφωνος.definition: speaking the same language with; of the same sound or tone, in unison with, A.Ag.158 . Adv. having the same name with, Str.9.2.29

ὁμοχοῖνιξ.definition: one who shares the same Plu.2.643d

ὁμόχορος.definition: belonging to the same chorus, ib.768b

ὁμοχροέω.definition: to be of the same colour, Gp.19.6.2, Aët.7.38

ὁμόχροια.definition: sameness of colour, X.Cyn.5.18; even surface of the body, skin, Hdt.1.74 ; so of inner and outer surfaces of skull, Hp.VC1; of surface of eye, Id.Carn.17: metaph., Pl.Ax.369d

ὁμοχρονέω.definition: keep time with, Luc.Im.14: abs., keep time, Id.Hist.Conscr.50

ὁμόχροος.definition: contr. of one colour, opp. Arist.HA543a25, cf. 525a4; alike in colour, prob. in Epicur.Ep.I p.IIU., cf.Gal.13.496, AP5.300 ; uniform in colour, Hp.Mul.1.40: heterocl.pl. Archig. ap. Paul.Aeg.4.5

ὁμόχρως.definition: gen. = foreg., Arist.GA749a22, Thphr.Sens.37, HP9.4.10, etc

ὁμόψηφος.definition: having an equal right to vote with, Hdt.6.109; Id.7.149

ὁμόω.definition: unite: Pass., =; = in fut. Med., Nic.Th.334

ὄμπνιος.definition: in codd. freq. of or; epith. of Demeter, Call.Aet.Oxy.2079.10; Nonn.D.11.213, cf. Hsch. s.v. prob. in IG22.1352 : then in late Poets, ib.14.1389i56, cf. BCH11.161

ὀμφακίας.definition: wine from unripe grapes; as masc. Adj., harsh, austere, Ar.Ach.352, cf. Plu.2.11d

ὀμφακίζω.definition: to be unripe, prop. of grapes, Gp.5.43.3; of a vine, bear sour grapes, LXXIs.18.5

ὀμφάκινος.definition: made from unripe grapes; a garment named prob. from its colour, Poll.7.56

ὀμφάκιον.definition: juice of unripe grapes, Dsc.5.5; = II.2, Aristaenet.2.7

ὀμφακίς.definition: cup of the acorn of Valonia oak, used for tanning, and as an astringent medicine, Paul.Aeg.3.42

ὀμφακίτης.definition: = Dsc.5.6; epith. of Dionysus, Ael.VH3.41; name of a green stone, prob. for in Gal.12.207:—fem. as Adj., unripe, Hp.Mul.2.195: as Subst., Aleppo gall, gall of Quercus infectoria, Dsc.1.107, Gal.8.114

ὀμφακόμελι.definition: drink of sour grapes and honey, Diocl.Fr.69, Dsc.5.23, Philagr. ap. Orib.5.19.4

ὀμφαλητομία.definition: cutting of the navel-string, midwifery, Pl.Tht.149e:—also Arist.HA587a9, Poll.4.208 , Sor.1.80

ὀμφαλητόμος.definition: cutting the navel-string: as Subst. midwife, Ion. word for Att. Hippon.12 Diehl, Hp.Mul.1.46: also Sophr.66

ὀμφαλιστήρ.definition: knife to cut the navel-string, Poll.2.169,4.208, Hsch

ὀμφαλοειδής.definition: like a navel or boss, Eust.1350.5

ὀμφαλόκαρπος.definition: bearing fruit like an name for Dsc.3.90

ὀμφή.definition: poet. Noun, voice, in Hom. always of the; sweet, tuneful voice, Pi.Fr.152; ib.75.19; . . Id.N.10.34, cf. S.Ichn.321

ὁμωνυμέω.definition: have the same name with, Ath.11.491c; have the same meaning with, A.D.Pron.105.31

ὁμωνυμία.definition: a having the same name, verbal identity; fraudulent use of an identity of name, POxy.257.44 , 1266.36

ὁμώνυμος.definition: is a misspelling; Subst., Pi.Fr.105, Hdt.3.67, Pl.Sph.218b, 234b; your namesake, Id.Prt.311b; Id.Tht.147d; Luc.Im.20

ὁμωροφέω.definition: to be under the same roof, v.l. in Aesop.10

ὁμωρόφιος.definition: being or lodging under the same roof with, Antipho5.11, D.18.287, 21.118: abs., Opp.H.5.418: is f.l. in codd., e.g. of Str.9.3.5, Gal.14.215

ὀνάγρινος.definition: like a wild ass, of the colour of a garment, BGU717.10 , cf. Poll.7.56

ὀνάλουμα.definition: late Thess. for foreg., ib.461.12 , al

ὀνάριον.definition: Dim. of Diph.89, Macho ap.Ath.13.582c, Arr.Epict.2.24.18, Vit.Aesop. Oxy.2083.19, POxy.63.11 ; of a bronze figure, PGiss.47.17

ὀνείδειος.definition: reproachful, with; dishonourable, of the fruits of begging, AP9.573

ὀνειδίζω.definition: without acc. rei, reproach, upbraid; c. dat. pers., Lys.27.16, etc.; Hdt.4.79; Id.8.92; without dat. pers., Il.7.95

ὀνειδισμός.definition: reproach, Ep. Rom.15.3 , al., J.AJ19.7.1, Plu.Art.22; calumny, Vett.Val.65.7, 73.10

ὀνειδιστής.definition: one who reproaches with a thing, c. gen. rei, Arist.Rh.1381b2

ὄνειδος.definition: reproach, rebuke, censure, blame; the statement of Eust.88.15, 647.36 that meant originally any report of one, reputation, character, is not borne out by the passages he cites— S.Ph.477; E.Ph.821 ; Id.Med.514, IA305, …

ὀνειραιτησία.definition: obtaining of revelations in a dream, PMag.Berol.1.329

ὀνειραιτητέω.definition: obtain revelations by means of a dream, PMag.Par.1.2077

ὀνειραιτητόν.definition: revelation obtained in a dream, ib.1.2501, PMag.Leid.V.6.15, PMag.Lond.121.222, 250

ὀνειραυτοπτέω.definition: or of an incantation, cause the operator to see a god in dreams, PMag.Par.1.2624 , 3179

ὀνειροδότης.definition: giver of dreams, Perdrizet- Lefèbvre Les graffites grecs du Memnonion d' Abydos No.493:—fem. cj. for in Poet.de herb.42

ὀνειροκρίτης.definition: interpreter of dreams, Thphr.Char.16.11, Theoc.21.33, SIG 1133 :—fem. IG3.162

ὀνειρολεκτέω.definition: talk in a dream, Sch.Arist.Id.p.344 Dind

ὀνειρολεσχία.definition: talking in dreams, ibid., dub. l. in Suid

ὀνειρόπληκτος.definition: scared by a dream, Hsch., Suid

ὀνειροπολέω.definition: pf. Phld.Mus.p.88 K.:—dream; cheat by dreams, Ar.Eq.809

ὀνειροπόλος.definition: interpreter of dreams; Adj. of or belonging to dreams, Orph.A.35,601

ὀνειροπομπέω.definition: send a dream or get a dream sent, PMag.Lond.46.488, PMag.Par.1.1869, 2077: c. acc. pers., ib.2451

ὀνειρόφρων.definition: versed in dreams and their interpretations, E.Hec.709

ὀνειρωγμός.definition: effusion during sleep, Dsc.3.132 , Ruf. ap. Orib.6.38.8 , Gal.4.598, etc

ὀνείρωξις.definition: dreaming, hallucination, Pl.Ti.52b; effusion in sleep, Sor.[2.46], Porph.Abst.4.20, Orib.Syn.9.38

ὀνειρώσσω.definition: Att. dream, Pl.Tht.158b; have an emission of semen during sleep, Hp.Morb.2.51, Ph.2.231, Philostr.Gym.49,52, Sch.Ar.Nu.16

ὀνεύω.definition: draw up with a windlass , impf. Th.7.25: generally, haul up, . . Stratt.30:—Med., Erot., Gal.19.126

ὀνηλασία.definition: driving of donkeys, D.Chr.10.19; post of public donkey-driver, POxy.2131.11 , cf. BGU15 ii 15 , PFlor.2.205,211

ὀνηλάσιον.definition: provision of stabling for donkeys, PRyl.183.2

ὀνηλάτης.definition: donkey-driver, Archipp.44, D.42.7, Crates Theb. ap. D.L.6.92, PLond.1.131.30 , Gal.10.134, etc

ὀνήσιμος.definition: useful, profitable, beneficial, h.Merc.30, A.Eu.924 ; S.Ant.995, cf. Aj.665, etc.; aiding, succouring, Id.Tr.1014 . Adv. Pl.Lg.747c

ὀνησίπολις.definition: Dor. profitable to the state, Simon.5.3

ὀνθύλευσις.definition: the use of forced meat, Men.462.7

ὀνθυλεύω.definition: dress with forced meat or stuffing, in; doctor wine, Sch.Ar.Pl.1064

ὀνίνημι.definition: Act., profit, benefit, help, and sts. gratify, delight, abs., . . Il.8.36, cf. Hes.Th.429, E.Med.533, etc.: with neut. Adj. or Adv., h.Merc.577; E.Heracl.705 , cf. Pl.Phlb.58c; Simon.55, Aret.CA1.4: c.acc. pers., Il.5…

ὀνίς.definition: ass's dung, Hp.Nat.Mul.82, Dsc.2.80, Gal.12.803: also in pl., Ar.Pax4, Arist.HA552a17; Hp.Mul.2.192 : but is strangely expld. horse's dung by Hsch., Phot., Suid

ὀνίσκος.definition: Dim. of but only metaph; a sea-fish of the gadus or cod kind, Dorio ap. Ath.3.118c, Euthyd. ap. eund.7.315f, Gal.6.721

ὀνοβατέω.definition: have a mare covered by an ass; of the ass, cover, Poll.5.92

ὀνοβάτις.definition: riding on an ass, of an adulteress who was thus punished at Cumae, Plu.2.291e, cf. Hsch

ὀνοβρυχίς.definition: a leguminous plant, cock's head, Onobrychis caput-galli, Dsc.3.153, Gal.12.89

ὀνοθήρας.definition: and oleander, Nerium Oleander, Thphr.HP9.19.1, Dsc.4.117

ὀνοκένταυρα.definition: a kind of demon haunting wild places, LXXIs.13.22, 34.11, 14

ὀνοκέφαλος.definition: with the head of an ass, Cyran.70, Horap.1.23

ὀνοκίνδιος.definition: donkey-driver, epith. of Peisander in Eup.182; in Hsch. also

ὀνοκτηνοτρόφος.definition: one who keeps donkeys, PTeb.564 , PLond.3.1165.6

ὀνόκωλος.definition: = of the hobgoblin Empusa, Sch.Ar.Ra.296:—also Eust.1704.42

ὀνομάζω.definition: impf. A.Ag.682 , etc.; Ep; of things, name, specify, Il.18.449; but also, name or promise, opp. giving, . . 9.515; use the term 'being', Pl.Tht.160b, cf. 166c, 201d; dedicate, Theopomp.Hist.121:—Pass., . . have been e…

ὄνομαι.definition: 2sg. Od.17.378; Ep. 2pl. Il.24.241; 3pl. Od.21.427, Hdt.2.167; opt. Il.13.287: impf. 3pl. Hdt.2.172: Ep. fut. Il.9.55, Od.5.379: aor. Il.14.95; Ep. part. 24.439: also Ep. aor. 3sg. 17.25; and Pass. Hdt.2.136; cf. find…

ὀνομαίνω.definition: h.Ven.290, Aeol. and Dor. GDI4992a; simply, utter, speak, Od.11.251, cf. h.Ven.290; then promise to do, Od.24.341

ὀνομακλήτωρ.definition: one who announces guests by name, Lat. nomenclator, Luc.Merc.Cond.10, Ath.2.47e

ὀνομασία.definition: name, Hippias1 J. , Pl.Plt.275d; nomination for office, POxy.1642.3 , 2130.12 , Jul.Mis.368b

ὀνομαστής.definition: autumator, Gloss; nominator of C. for the BGU96.9

ὀνομάτιον.definition: Dim. of Longin.43.2, Arr.Epict.2.23.14: without dim. sense, POxy.2131.9

ὀνοματογραφία.definition: writing of names, LXX1 Es.6.12, S.E.M.11.67

ὀνοματοθεσία.definition: the giving a name, nomenclature, Eust.39.23

ὀνοματοθετέω.definition: give a name, Olymp.in Cat.105.16, Eust.32.6; cj. for in Arist.APo.83a14

ὀνοματοθέτης.definition: one who gives a name, namer, v.l. in recc. for Pl.Chrm.175b

ὀνοματολόγος.definition: collector of words, Ath.9.397a; one who tells people's names, Lat. nomenclator, Plu.Cat.Mi.8

ὀνοματομάχος.definition: fighting about a word, expression, or name, Critol. ap. Clem.Al.Strom.2.7.33.1

ὀνοματοποιέω.definition: coin names, Arist.Cat.7a5, EN1108a18, Top.104b36, Phld.Mus.p.54 K., Ph.1.602, S.E.M.1.314, Gal.2.736

ὀνοματοποίησις.definition: the coining of a name or word, Suid. s.v

ὀνοματοποιία.definition: the coining of a word in imitation of a sound, Str.14.2.28, Quint.Inst.1.5.72: pl., Plu.2.747d

ὀνοματοποιός.definition: coiner of names, esp. significant names, Ath.3.99c, Zos.Alch.p.230 B

ὀνοματουργία.definition: the making of names, ib.p.44 P

ὀνόπορδον.definition: pellitory, Parietaria cretica, Epich.161, Plin.HN 27.110, Hsch

ὀνοπρόσωπος.definition: ass-faced, Herm. Trism. in Rev.Phil.32.256, Sch.Luc.Sacr.14

ὀνοτάζω.definition: like blame, h.Merc.30; Hes.Op.258:— Med., abominating it, A.Supp.10 codd

ὀνοχειλές.definition: Cretan bugloss, Echium parviflorum, Ps.-Dsc.4.23 , Plin.HN22.51:—also Aët.1.5, Paul.Aeg.7.3 p.187 H

ὀνόχηλον.definition: as if from ass's hoof, Sch.Nic.Th.838 ; cf

ὀνυχιαῖος.definition: of a nail's breadth, Eust.ad D.P.Prooem.p.73.31 B

ὀνυχίζω.definition: pare the nails. in Med., Jul.Mis.339b; to have the hoof cloven, LXXLe.11.7, al

ὀνυχιμαῖος.definition: of the size of nail-parings, diminutive, Com.Adesp.879

ὀνύχινος.definition: made of onyx, IG; like onyx, Plin.HN15.55; esp. onyx-coloured, of garments, POxy.114.6 , 1026.10 ; PGen.68.6

ὀνύχιον.definition: Dim. of I, small claw; pig's trotters, Sammelb.1941 , PLond.3.1259.37

ὀνυχιστήριον.definition: nail-knife or scissors, Posidipp.38; = unguicularium, Gloss

ὀνυχίτης.definition: of the onyx kind, Dsc.5.74:—also fem. App.Mith.115, cf. Plin. HN34.103

ὀνυχογραφέομαι.definition: Pass., to be scored with the nail, Hp.Epid.6.6.4

ὀνυχόπαχος.definition: of the thickness of a finger-nail, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.48 B

ὀνυχοφόρος.definition: carrying the nails, of the last phalanx of the finger, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.238.26

ὀνυχόω.definition: make like a nail, claw, or hook, the claw-shaped side of the scalpel, Orib.46.11.18; has horny hoofs, Sch.Ar.Ra.232

ὀξαλίς.definition: sour wine, Hsch; sorrel, Rumex acetosa, Nic.Th.840; = Ps.-Dsc.2.114

ὀξίδιον.definition: Dim. of PCair.Zen.527.9 : written in Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.21, Suid.: pl. Sammelb. 4425 vii 20 , BGU417.31

ὀξίζω.definition: taste or smell like vinegar, Dsc.1.115.2, 5.6, Gp.3.7.1 , Archig. ap. Gal.13.218, etc

ὀξίνης.definition: sharp, sour, Plu.2.913b; metaph., sour-tempered, tart, Ar.Eq.1304; Id.V.1082.—In Gp.6.4.2 and Phryn.PSp.92 B., we find v.l. in Gp. l.c

ὀξίς.definition: vinegar-cruet, Nicostr.Com.9; a measure, at Athens the same as but at Cleonae, = Id.Fr.688, Diph.96

ὀξυάκανθα.definition: fiery thorn, Cotoneaster Pyracantha, Dsc.1.93, Gal.6.643:—also Thphr.HP1.9.3, 3.3.1, Gal.12.90

ὀξύβαρις.definition: circumflex accent, Ammonius in Gramm.Lat.4.531 K.; called in Arc.188.4

ὀξυβάφιον.definition: Dim. of sq., Antiph.163.5, POxy.1657.7 ; Stud.Pal.20.67.10

ὀξύβαφον.definition: small vinegar-saucer: then; as a measure, the fourth part of a about 1/8 of a pint, Alex.172.11, cf. Thphr.HP9.11.7, al., Nic.Th.598, Dsc.3.27. , PMed.Strassb.p.7 K., is condemned by Phryn.PSp.97 B.)

ὀξυβελής.definition: shooting sharp-pointed, and therefore swift, missiles, opp. Ph.Bel.54.49; with and without an engine for throwing sharp-pointed bolts, opp. D.S.20.85,86; so , ib.75, etc

ὀξύβλαττα.definition: in Lat. form oxyblatta, bright purple, Cod.Just.4.40.1

ὀξυβλέπτης.definition: one who is sharp-sighted, Hsch. s.v. Gloss

ὀξυβόας.definition: and shrill-screaming, of birds, A.Ag.57; of men, Luc.JTr.31; sharp-buzzing, of mosquitoes, AP5.150

ὀξύγαλα.definition: sour milk, whey, . . Ctes.Fr.57.22, cf. Str.7.4.6, Plu.Art.3, Gal.6.689

ὀξυγαλάκτινος.definition: made of sour milk, ib.697, 12.272, cf. 6.518

ὀξύγαρον.definition: sauce of vinegar and Arr.Epict.2.20.30, Gal.6.534, Ath.2.67e, 9.366c:—also Gloss., condemned by Phryn.PSp.97 B

ὀξύγλυκυ.definition: drink of acidulated honey, Hp.Fract.11 , 36 , etc.:—so Gal.18.466; Lat.dulcacidum, Gloss

ὀξυγώνιος.definition: acute-angled, Arist.Top.107a17, Cael.307a2, Euc.1Def.21, Onos.10.16: neut. as Subst., acute-angled body, Epicur.Ep.2p.50U

ὀξυδερκέω.definition: prob. f.l. for Ph.1.409, 2.480, Hsch. s.v

ὀξυδερκής.definition: sharp-sighted, quick-sighted; Act., promoting quickness of sight, Diocl.Fr.128, cf. Dsc.5.5, Gal.12.263, al

ὀξυδερκία.definition: sharp-sightedness, Epicur.Nat.28Fr.6, cf. Apollod.3.10.3, Gal.14.241, Alex.Aphr.in Top.258.17, etc.: Ion. Democr.119

ὀξυδορκέω.definition: to be quick of sight, Arist.Rh.Al.1421a22, Com.Adesp.359, Str.6.2.1, etc.; v

ὀξυδορκία.definition: = Andronic.Rhod.p.572 M., Hippod. ap. Stob.4.39.26, Plot.5.9.1, etc

ὀξυέθειρ.definition: gen. with sharp points, nom. pl. Marc.Sid.35; acc. pl. Nonn.D.14.368; gen.sg. ib.22.25

ὀξυέλαιον.definition: mixture of oil and vinegar, Gal.13.397

ὀξυηκοΐα.definition: Dor. a sharp, quick ear, Hippod. ap. Stob.4.39.26, Metop. ib.3.1.115, Plu.2.34c, Alex.Aphr.in Top.327.14, interpol. in Poll.2.82

ὀξυήκοος.definition: quick of hearing : of quick perception, keen, Pl.Ti.75b; Arist.HA534a6, cf. A.D.Synt.295.23.—In codd. sts. wrongly Comp. Luc.Pr.Im.20, Porph.Abst.3.8: Sup. prob. l. in S.E.M.9.65, for

ὀξυθάνατος.definition: dying quickly, short-lived; killing quickly, Str.17.2.4

ὀξύθηκτος.definition: sharp-edged, sharp-pointed; of a person, goaded to passion, infuriated, S.Ant.1301

ὀξυθυμέω.definition: to be quick to anger, E.Andr.689; Pass., to be provoked, Ar.V.501, cf. Th.466; to be irritable, Gal.15.598

ὀξυθυμία.definition: vivacity or instability of temper, Hp.Epid.2.4.4, E.Andr.728, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.6.5; excitability, Aret.SD1.5, cf. Poll.2.231

ὀξυθυμίας.definition: one who is quick to anger, Poll.2.231, 6.124

ὀξύθυμον.definition: a kind of thyme, PLille58 ii 21, iii 10

ὀξύθυμος.definition: quick to anger, choleric, Epich.281. E.Med.319, Ar.V.406,455, 1105, Arist.Rh.1368b20, LXXPr.14.17, al.; sharp to punish, of the Areopagus, A.Eu.705; by crasis = E.Ba.671, Men.Georg.Fr.3

ὀξυκαμπής.definition: sharply curved, of hooks, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.18.13

ὀξυκέφαλος.definition: with pointed head, Poll.2.43, Philum.Ven.31.1, Sch.Ar.Av.1295

ὀξυκινησία.definition: quickness of motion, Ptol.Tetr.19, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.12, Eun.VSp.473 B., Lyd.Mens.2.9

ὀξυκίνητος.definition: quickly moving, Luc.Abd.28, Dips.5; Ph.1.605; of tumours, etc., Cass.Pr.1

ὀξυκόμμι.definition: a kind of gum, in the form , PMag.Osl.1.74

ὀξύκομος.definition: with pointed hair, of the porcupine, Opp.C.2.599; of a stag, ib.194; of a pine, App.Anth.5.46; with pointed spines, of a fish, Marc.Sid.21

ὀξύκρατον.definition: Ion. sour wine mixed with water, Dsc.2.105, Aret.CA1.1, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.18.31, 4.11.14, Erot. s.v. Gal.11.439, al., Aët.15.1

ὀξυλάβεια.definition: quickness in seizing an opportunity, Eust.123.46; cf

ὀξυλαβέω.definition: seize quickly : seize an opportunity, X.HG7.4.27, Men.Epit.528, Gal.Parv.Pil.3

ὀξυλάβη.definition: a kind of tongs, Suid. s.v

ὀξυλαβής.definition: quick at seizing, of the eagle, Arist.HA619b29

ὀξυλαβία.definition: quickness in seizing an opportunity, Sch.T Il.10.204, Sch.A.Th.97; cf

ὀξυλάπαθον.definition: curled dock, Rumex crispus, Dsc.2.114, Gal.6.635, al., Aret.CA2.2, etc.: also Gp.2.5.4

ὀξυλίπαρος.definition: composed of vinegar and oil, Timocl.3.2; Sotad.Com.1.19

ὀξυλιπὴς ἄρτος.definition: bread dressed with vinegar and fat, Gal.10.575

ὀξυλοβέω.definition: have sharp ears, hear sharply, Suid

ὀξυμάθεια.definition: quickness at learning, Str.2.3.5, with v.l

ὀξυμαθής.definition: learning quickly, Phryn.PSp.97 B., Suid. s.v

ὀξύμαλον Περσικόν.definition: Lacon. for peach, Prunus persica, Ar.Byz. ap. Ath.3.83a, Hsch

ὀξυμελίκρατον.definition: Ion. mixture of vinegar and honey, oxymel, Hp.Loc.Hom.17:—also Id.Acut.19,59, Lys.Fr.42, Arist.Pr.922a6, cf. Dsc.5.14, Gal.15.677

ὀξυμήνιτος.definition: perh. bringing down quick anger , A.Eu.472

ὀξυμυρσίνη.definition: = butcher's broom, Ruscus aculeatus, Dsc.4.144, cf. 1.11, Androm. ap. Gal.13.842, Gal.6.643; also called Plin.HN15.27, 23.165

ὀξύμωρος.definition: pointedly foolish: a witty saying, the more pointed from being paradoxical or seemingly absurd, such as insaniens sapientia, strenua inertia, splendide mendax, Serv.ad Verg.A.7.295, etc

ὀξύνιτρον.definition: mixture of vinegar and soda, Paul.Aeg.5.4

ὀξυντήρ.definition: sharpener, i.e.a penknife, AP6.64 , cf. Aq.Jb.41.22

ὀξύνω.definition: fut. LXXWi.5.20, D.2.11; metaph., goad to anger, provoke, S.l.c.:—Pass., Hdt.8.138, cf. LXXEz.21.9

ὀξυόδους.definition: with sharp teeth; in Nonn.D.40.484, with a neut.Subst. with beechen shaft, beechen, Il.5.568, cf. 50, etc.; 14.443, cf. Eust.1951.2, Hsch.: the deriv. from is less probable

ὀξύπεινος.definition: ravenously hungry, ravenous, greedy, of the eagle, Arist.HA619b29; of persons, Antiph.276, Eub.10.4: metaph., Plu.2.512f, cf. Cic.Att.2.12.2:—later of one who eats between meals, Anon.in EN182.9; Procl.ad Hes.Op.522

ὀξυπέπερι.definition: mixture of vinegar and pepper, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.84

ὀξύπικρος.definition: keen, smarting, Hsch. s.v. = acidus, Gloss

ὀξύπληκτος.definition: struck by a sharp blow, cj. in S.Ant.1301

ὀξυποδητής.definition: one who quickens his pace, ib

ὀξυπολυφαγία.definition: quickness of eating and digesting, ib

ὀξυπόρος.definition: with pointed mouth, Opp.H.2.406; quick-passing, active, of medicines, Dsc.3.51

ὀξύπρῳρος.definition: sharp-prowed : sharp-pointed, A.Pr.423 ; Opp.H.3.333: to be written with iota, Achae. ap. Lex.Mess.p.408

ὀξύπτερος.definition: sharp- or swift-winged: as Subst. = Ps.-Dsc.4.52; but, hawk, Clem.Al.Strom.5.8.52.1 :—also = falco, Gloss.; swift wings, Aesop.8

ὀξυπύθμενος.definition: with pointed bottom, of shell-fish, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.85

ὀξύπυκνος.definition: in the higher region of the , Cleonid.Harm.4,9, Bacch.Harm.27, cf. Aristid.Quint.1.6

ὀξυπώγων.definition: gen. with a pointed beard, Heph.Astr.2.2

ὀξυρεγμία.definition: the peevishness or fretfulness caused thereby, Ar.Fr.473; cf

ὀξυρεγμιάω.definition: to be troubled with heartburn, Dsc.3.30, 4.1, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.8.3

ὀξυρεπής.definition: = with quick-turning art. Pi.O.9.91; in Hsch

ὀξυρρόδινον.definition: rose-oil mixed with vinegar, Ath.2.67f, Gal.11.559, Gloss

ὀξύρροπος.definition: turning quickly, prop. of a delicate balance : metaph., sudden and quick to anger, Pl.Tht.144a; Jul.Or.2.65d; Memn.2; also unstable temper, Pl.R.411b; rapidity or vehemence, Longin.18.1; cf. Adv. D.C.Fr.50.3

ὀξυρρυγχιτικόν.definition: a measure of capacity in Egypt, PLond.3.1170v.79 , PGiss.34.12

ὀξύρρυγχος.definition: sharp-snouted: metaph., sharp-; Subst., a sharp-snouted Egyptian fish, [Hes.] ap.Ath.3.116b, Str.17.2.4, Ael.NA10.46, Ath.7.312b

ὀξύστερνος.definition: sharp-breasted, of animals as compared with man, Gal.18.536

ὀξύστομος.definition: sharp-beaked, of gryphons, A.Pr.803; of; of a sword, sharp-edged, E.Supp.1206; of a cupping instrument, sharp-rimmed, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.15

ὀξύσχοινος.definition: great sea-rush, Juncus acutus, Batr.164, Dsc.4.52, Gal.12.136

ὀξυτελής.definition: with sharp ends, diamond shaped, of open spaces in lattice-work, dub.l. in Lyd.Mag.3.37

ὀξυτονέω.definition: pronounce with an acute accent, i. e. on; in Music, make high-pitched, Nicom.Harm.10

ὀξυτόνησις.definition: a pronouncing with an acute accent, Eust.60.13

ὀξύτονος.definition: sharp-sounding, piercing. of sound; sung to a high note, D.H.Comp.11; having the acute accent, Hermog.Id.1.12, A.D.Pron.33.24, al. Adv. ib.29.2, S.E.M.1.222, Eust.41.4

ὀξυτόρος.definition: piercing, pointed, the pine with its sharp spines, AP4.1.16

ὀξύφαγρος.definition: a kind of a sea-fish, v.l. in Opp.H.1.140

ὀξύφυλλος.definition: with pointed leaves, Dsc.4.23; = Id.3.109, Gal.12.144

ὀξυφωνέω.definition: to have a shrill voice, Id.16.607; pronounce with an acute accent, Eust.23.4

ὁσαπλασίων.definition: gen. as many times as, Arist.Pr.929b14, Euc.12.13, Archim.Aequil.1.6

ὁσιωτήρ.definition: consecrator, the name given at Delphi to the victim offered when one of the priests called was appointed, Plu.2.292d

ὀσμάομαι.definition: older form , smell at a; metaph., perceive, remark, S.Fr.176

ὀσμή.definition: Att. form of the older , smell; the sense of smell, = Democr.11, Hsch.—The older form is alone used by Hom., Hdt., and Pi.; it occurs also in A.Pr.115 , Democr. l. c., and in later Prose, Thphr.CP6.14.1, al., Phylarch…

ὀσμύλη.definition: a strong-smelling musky octopus, Eledone cirrosa, Arist.Fr.305

ὀσμύλος.definition: = foreg., Id. ap. Ath.7.318e, Ael.NA5.44, Opp.H.1.307,310

ὀσμύλιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Ar.Fr.247, Call.Fr.38; = Hsch.: prob. to be read for in Gal.19.89 s.v

ὄσπρεον.definition: later spelling of POxy.494.10 , etc., rejected by EM635.48

ὀσπριοθήκη.definition: a place to keep pulse in, Gloss

ὀσπριοπώλης.definition: one who deals in pulse, IG22.1558.67: fem. Sch.Ar.Pl.427

ὄσσομαι.definition: Ep. Verb, used only in pres. and impf; see in spirit or with the mind's eye, Od.1.115, cf. 20.81

ὀσταναβολεύς.definition: and names of surgical instruments, Hermes 38.284 , 282

ὀστεογενής.definition: produced in the bones: epith. applied to the marrow, Pl. ap. Arist.Top.140a5

ὀστεοκόπος.definition: an inflammatory attack, which makes one feel asif one's bones were giving way, Hp.Acut.1 , Thphr.Lass.2, Gal.8.104, al.: in Com.Adesp.329, Gal.6.194

ὀστεολογία.definition: Ion. extraction of bones; description of bones, Ruf.Oss.1, Gal.14.720:—but Id.2.220

ὀστεολόγος.definition: extracting bones: a surgical instrument, Hp.Mul.1.70

ὀστοθηκάριον.definition: Dim. of sq., Wood Ephesus Append. 14

ὀστοθήκη.definition: receptacle for bones, sarcophagus, Lyc.367, Com.Adesp.329, IPE12.542.3 , CIG2728, 2731

ὀστολογία.definition: gathering up of bones after the burning

ὀστολόγος.definition: collecting bones, Epil.7; name of a tragedy by Aeschylus, Ath.15.667c

ὀστομάχιον.definition: a game played with fourteen pieces of bone, Aus.Opusc.17 Praef

ὀστοφανέω.definition: show bones, i. e. ribs, Hippiatr.38

ὀστοφυής.definition: of a bony nature or substance, Batr.296

ὀστρακίας.definition: a stone resembling an agate, Plin.HN37.177

ὀστράκινος.definition: earthen, made of clay, of; like earthenware, = v.l. in Luc.Lex.6

ὀστρακίτης.definition: fem. an inferior variety of Dsc.5.74, Plin.HN 37.151; a kind of cake, Ath.14.647f

ὀστρακόδερμος.definition: with a shell like a potsherd, hard-shelled, Batr.295; testaceans or molluscs , opp. Arist.HA523b9, cf. 590a19, Thphr.HP4.6.8, Ath.3.89f, Jul.Or.6.193b; also of certain crabs, Arist.HA601a18; of eggs, ib.489b14

ὀστρακοκονία.definition: pavement made of crushed potsherds, concrete, Gp.2.27.5

ὀστρακόνωτος.definition: having the back covered with a hard shell, Teucer ap.Ath.10.455e, Ael.NA9.6

ὄστρεον.definition: or oyster; the proper Att. form; oyster- or bivalve-shell, Arist.HA531b5, 590a32

ὀσφραίνομαι.definition: fut. Ar.Pax152: aor. 2; metaph., get scent of, Id.Lys.619; Luc.Tim.45

ὄσφρησις.definition: the sense of smell, Pl.Phd.111b (as; the organ of smell, Arist.de An.425a5, Pr.907b28, 1 Ep.Cor.12.17, PRyl.63.5 ; Hdn.1.12.2

ὀσφυαλγής.definition: suffering from lumbago, A.Fr.361, cf. Hp.Coac.313

ὀτλέω.definition: suffer, endure, c. acc., Call.Fr.274, A.R.3.769, Lyc.819, etc.: abs., A.R.4.1227

ὄτοβος.definition: any loud noise, as the din of battle, Hes.Th.709; rattling of chariots, A.Th.151, 204 ; crash of thunder, S.OC1479 ; also of the flute, Id.Aj.1202 : pl., Antim.Eleg.Fr.17.—The freq. Mss. reading is disproved by the metre

ὀτρυντύς.definition: a cheering on, exhortation, Il.19.234, 235, Antim.91

ὀτρύνω.definition: Ep. inf. Il.4.286: impf; less freq. of animals, urge on, cheer on, 23.111; 16.167, etc.; 18.584

ὀττεύομαι.definition: regard as ominous, D.H.9.23, 55: hence, deprecate as ill-omened, Id.2.19.—The Act. prob. f.l. in Ael.NA3.9 : was the equiv. Hellenic form, acc. to Moer. l. c

οὐδενία.definition: or nothingness, worthlessness, Pl.Phdr.235a, Tht.176c, Ephor.137 J., Plb.34.14.3, Ph.1.477, Ael.NA15.13, etc

οὐλαμοεργός.definition: = foreg., epith. of the planet Mars, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.173

οὐλαμός.definition: throng of warriors, esp. in battle, in; later as a t.t., troop of cavalry, Plb.6.28.3, al., Plu.Lyc.23

οὐλαμώνυμος.definition: named from the armed throng , epith. of Neoptolemus, Lyc.183

οὐλοδέτης.definition: sheaf of barley, Eust.1162.33:—also straw-band for binding sheaves, ib.30

οὐλομελής.definition: sound of limb, prob. f.l. in Parm.8.4

οὐλόφρων.definition: gen. = restd. by Valck. in A.Supp.750 for

οὐλοχοεῖον.definition: or the vessel in which the sacred barley was kept, Hsch

οὐραία.definition: = Aret.CD2.13, Hdn.Gr.1.531, Eust.1758.56; in Babr.110.3, is perh. f.l. for

οὐρανοβατέω.definition: walk or move in heaven, Vett. Val.241.14

οὐρανογνώμων.definition: gen. skilled in the heavens, Luc.Icar.5, Eust.1337.18

οὐρανογραφία.definition: Ion. description of the heavens, title of a work by Democritus, D.L.9.48

οὐρανοδρόμος.definition: running along the sky, Tab.Defix.Aud. 41 B5

οὐρανοκευθμωνοδίαιτος.definition: dwelling in the recesses of heaven, PMag.Par.1.1351

οὐρανοκλῖμαξ.definition: ladder reaching to heaven, v.l. in Ph.1.620

οὐρανοπετής.definition: fallen from heaven, Plu.2.83 of, cf. 870c

οὐρανοπολίτης.definition: citizen of heaven, attributed to Plato by Anon.Proll.Plat.10 , cf. Phlp.in de An.563.8

οὐρανόροφος.definition: with vaulted ceiling or canopy, prob. cj. for in Ath.1.48f; v. sq.II

οὐρανοῦχος.definition: holding heaven, the rule of heaven, A.Ch.960

οὐρανοφάντωρ.definition: shining up to heaven; or disclosing heaven, Suid

οὐρανοφοίτης.definition: walking in heaven, Hymn.Mag.2..14, Suid. s.v. etc

οὐρανόφοιτος.definition: soaring in the sky, v.l. for Ph.2.513

οὐρανόω.definition: remove to heaven, deify, in Pass., Eust.17.34

οὐρεσιβώτης.definition: poet. for feeding on the mountains, S.Ph.1148

οὐρεύω.definition: to be on garrison duty, SIG527.127 ; cf

οὐρέω.definition: impf. D.54.4; Ion; c. acc. rei, pass with the water, Hp.Aph.4.80,81; Ant.Lib.41:— Pass., = Hp.Coac.584, etc.; is more diuretic, Id.Vict.2.46, cf. Ath.1.32f, Orib.inc.4.28; diuretic wine, Aret.CD1.4

οὐρητήρ.definition: in earlier writers, =; later, in pl., the ducts which convey the urine from the kidneys into the bladder, Gal.19.363, UP5.5

οὐρίζω.definition: Att. fut. carry with a fair wind, waft on the way, of words and prayers, A.Ch.317 ; speed on the way, guide prosperously, S.OT695 : an acc. may be supplied in A.Pers.602

οὐσιάζω.definition: make magically efficacious by applying an PMag.Lond.121.463

οὐσιάρχης.definition: source of existence, substantiae auctor, Apul.Asclep.19

οὐσιομετρία.definition: f. l. in Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

οὐσιοπάτωρ.definition: father of existence, of the Second God, Iamb.Myst.8.2

οὐσιότης.definition: the quality of existence, Dam.Pr.58, Eliasin Cat.221.1; substantiality, Corp.Herm.12.1, Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.4

οὐτάω.definition: sts. generally, wound, like with lightning, E.Hipp.684; Id.HF199, cf. Opp.H.2.372

οὔτι πω.definition: Ion. not at all yet, v

ὀφειλέω.definition: = in Pass., to be due, dub; in Act., to be bound to . . , c. inf., dub. l. in Id.48

ὀφειλή.definition: debt, X.Vect. , Ostr.Bodl.i 311; one's due, Ep.Rom.13.7, 1 Ep.Cor.7.3

ὀφείλημα.definition: that which is owed, debt, Th.2.40, etc.; Pl.Lg.717b; Arist.EN1165a3: also in Inscrr., IG12.57.14, SIG306.38 , 1108.11 , etc.; and Pap., PHib.1.42.10 , etc.; cf

ὀφεόδηκτος.definition: bitten by a serpent, Eust.330.12:—written Tz.H.8 No.170 tit

ὀφθαλμία.definition: Ion. ophthalmia, a disease of; metaph., Phld.Vit.p.21 J

ὀφθαλμίας.definition: quick-sight, a kind of eagle; a kind of fish, Plaut.Cap.850

ὀφθαλμίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be inoculated or engrafted, of; to be set with precious stones, etc., Suid

ὀφθαλμῖτις.definition: epith. of Athena as goddess of the Moon, Paus.3.18.1

ὀφθαλμοβολέω.definition: cast the eyes upon an object, Sch.Il.3.443

ὀφθαλμοβόρος.definition: picking out eyes, of the heron, Arist.HA617a9

ὀφθαλμοειδής.definition: like eyes, Dsc.3.139. Adv; visible, Aristox.Harm.p.40 M

ὀφθαλμοκλέπτης.definition: stealer of the eye , Tz. ad Lyc.843

ὀφθαλμόσοφος.definition: skilled in the eyes, an oculist, Luc.Lex.4

ὀφθαλμοφανής.definition: apparent to the eye, visible, Arist.Fr.208; . . PHib.1.89.8 ; obvious, Str.2.1.18; Aristox.Harm.p.41 M. Adv. LXXEs.8.13, Ph.1.614, S.E.M.9.39, Cleom.2.6

ὀφθαλμωρυχέω.definition: gouge out the eyes, Phld.Hom.p.59 O

ὀφίασις.definition: bald place on the head, of serpentine; a form of leprosy in which the patient sheds his skin like a snake, Ps.-Gal.14.757

ὀφιογενής.definition: serpent-gendered: a name of some Asiatic tribes, Crates Gramm. ap. Plin.HN7.13, Varro ap. Priscian.Inst.10.32, Str.13.1.14, Ael.NA12.39, etc

ὀφιόδηκτος.definition: bitten by a serpent, LXXSi.12.13, Gal.14.300, Hippiatr.86, Sch.Il.2.722, etc

ὀφιοκτόνη.definition: serpent-killer, a kind of prob. for in Dsc.Ther.5

ὀφιομάχος.definition: fighting with serpents, Ph.1.86: as Subst., a kind of locust, and the ichneumon, Hsch.:—in the former sense is found in LXXLe.11.22, Ph.1.39

ὀφιόνεος.definition: of, belonging to, or like a serpent, Opp.C.2.237, 3.436 [where

ὀφιοπαίκτης.definition: snake-charmer, Lat. praestigiator, prob. cj. for Gloss

ὀφιόπους.definition: with serpents for legs, Luc.Philops.22, Suid

ὀφιοπρόσωπος.definition: with serpent face, dub. cj. in Sch. Veron. Verg.A.7.341

ὀφιόσπαρτος.definition: poet. sown or engendered by serpents, EM287.13

ὀφιοφάγος.definition: serpent-eating: name of a people, Plin. HN6.169

ὀφρυάζω.definition: signify anything with the eyebrows; to be haughty, supercilious, Phryn.PSp.93B., Procop.Goth.4.11,28, Arc.16, Suid

ὀφρυανασπασίδης.definition: one who raises his eyebrows in scorn, Epigr. ap. Hegesand.2

ὀφρυάω.definition: to have ridges or hills, proverb. in Str.8.6.23; cf

ὀφρυόομαι.definition: Pass., to be supercilious, Timo29, S.E.P.3.278, Alciphr.3.4; full of supercilious rudeness, Luc.Am.2. is quadrisyll. in Timo l.c.]

ὀφρυόσκιος.definition: shaded by the eyebrows, Pl. ap. Arist.Top.140a4

ὀφρύωσις.definition: rim of socket of thigh-bone, Paul.Aeg.6.118

ὀχέτευμα.definition: = duct or passage of the nose, Arist.HA492b16

ὀχετηγέω.definition: conduct by ditches or conduits, Eust.1379.49

ὀχετηγία.definition: irrigation by ditches, Suid., v.l. in Procop.Goth.4.12

ὀχετόκρανον.definition: end or issue of an aqueduct, Hyp.Fr.132, Mnemos. 42.332 :—Dim. EM644.48, AB287

ὀχευτής.definition: = I.1, PCair.Zen.529 , Hsch. s.v. Dsc.2.79, Gal.6.533, Hippiatr.14: metaph., lewd person, lecher, AP11.318 , Corn.ND27

ὀχεύω.definition: of male animals, cover; c. acc., mount, cover, Pl.Euthd.298e, etc

οὔπως.definition: or Ion. Hdt.1.33:—Adv. no-how, in no wise, not at all, giving the greatest possible strength to the negation, Il.4.320, etc.; separated, 2.203, 4.158, etc

οὐρανόθεν.definition: Adv. from heaven, down from heaven, Od.5.294, Hes.Th.761, LXX4 Ma.4.10, JRS17.49 : joined with Preps., Il.21.199, Od.11.18, Hes.Sc.384; Il.8.19, 21, 17.548; Orph.L.601

οὐρανόθι.definition: Adv. in heaven, in the heavens, Il.3.3, expld. by Sch.A as = ; v.l

οὔτε.definition: Adv., joining neg. clauses, as joins; mostly repeated, . . , . . neither . . , nor . . , Lat. neque . . , neque . . , Hom., etc.—Hom. freq. joins another Particle with the first or second as . . , . .; . . , . .; . . …

οὔτοι.definition: or Adv. indeed not, Il.1.298, 515, 3.65, 4.29, Hes.Op.759, etc.: in Att. freq. before protestations, Ar.Pl.64; . . Id.V.1366; Id.Pax188; Id.Th.34; Id.V.1141 ; . . S.El.137 , etc.; Pl.Cri.43d; . . Id.Euthphr.2a, etc.; …

ὄφ.definition: exclamation of pain or fear accompanied by a sudden drawing in of breath, Eust.900.27

ὀφειλόντως.definition: Adv. part. of as of debt, deservedly, Hsch. s.v

ὄφρα.definition: used as a Final and Temporal Conj., correlat. to; after primary tenses and imper., Il.1.524, 4.205, al.; so also 22.382, etc.; Od.17.10, 18.364; Il.1.118, etc.; 2.440; so . . for 6.308, etc.; so also . . Pi.O.7.15; . …

ὄχα.definition: Ep. Adv., used by Hom. only as intens. before the Sup. far the best, Il.1.69, al.; cf

ὀψέ.definition: Aeol. , Adv. after a long time, at; it is not long since . . , Th.1.14
